insertion profiles with zero failures.  These bounded counts replay
the identities; the support-uniform proof is the displayed fusion and
spectral argument.
For a factor word of root support `n>=2`, the uniform upper-radial
corollary and this lemma reduce the unresolved lower band from
`n(n-1)` columns to

```text
n(n-1)-1,
```

namely `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S3BP)` with `(A,L)=(1,0)` removed.

The next antidiagonal has a uniform spectral chamber and a complete
arbitrary-label two-factor base.

**Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECONDTHR
(second lower-radial spectral threshold).**  Suppose

```text
C=sum_(h>=0)c_h beta_h>=0                 on [-1,3],
c_0>0,
```

and put `lambda=c_1/c_0`.  If

```text
3c_1^2-4c_0c_1-8c_0^2>=0,                      (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4H)
```

then

```text
K_(2,0)
 =c_0(c_2+c_3+c_4)-c_1c_3>=0.                  (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4I)
```

In particular this applies to every factor word whose doubled
coefficient profile satisfies `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4H)`.

**Proof.**  Under normalized `SO(3)` Haar measure put

```text
dnu=C(x)dmu/c_0,                   y=x-lambda.
```

This is a probability measure and `integral y dnu=0`.  The ordinary
character recurrence gives

```text
beta_3(x)=x^3-2x^2-x+1,
```

while `x beta_3=beta_2+beta_3+beta_4`.  Consequently

```text
K_(2,0)
 =c_0^2 Cov_nu(x,beta_3(x)),                    (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4J)

Cov_nu(x,beta_3(x))
 =integral y^2{
    y^2+(3lambda-2)y+3lambda^2-4lambda-1
   }dnu.                                        (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4K)
```

The minimum on the whole real line of the quadratic in braces is

```text
(3lambda^2-4lambda-8)/4.
```

Condition `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4H)` makes this nonnegative.
Therefore the integrand in `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4K)` is pointwise
nonnegative, proving `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4I)`.  QED.

**Corollary 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECOND2F
(one--two-factor second radial base).**  If

```text
P=product_(j=1)^m chi_(a_j),             a_j>=1,
P^2=sum_(h>=0)c_h beta_h,
```

and `m<=2`, then `K_(2,0)>=0`, uniformly in the labels.

**Proof.**  For one factor the profile is `1_[0,a_1]`, and direct
substitution gives the margins

```text
0, 1, 1, 2
```

for `a_1=1`, `a_1=2`, `a_1=3`, and `a_1>=4`, respectively.

For two factors write `1<=a<=b` and `delta=b-a`.  Since

```text
chi_a^2=sum_(t=0)^a beta_t,
chi_b^2=sum_(s=0)^b beta_s,
```

ordinary fusion gives the exact low-shell count

```text
c_r=sum_(t=0)^a
 # {s:0<=s<=b, |t-s|<=r<=t+s}

   =sum_(t=0)^a
 max(0,min(b,t+r)-|t-r|+1).                     (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4L)
```

For `a>=4`, substitution at `r=0,...,4` gives

```text
delta     (c_0,c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4)                    K_(2,0)

0       (a+1,3a,  5a-4,7a-11,9a-21)             18(a-2)
1       (a+1,3a+1,5a-2,7a-8, 9a-17)             11a-19
2       (a+1,3a+1,5a-1,7a-6, 9a-14)             11a-15
3       (a+1,3a+1,5a-1,7a-5, 9a-12)             11a-13
>=4     (a+1,3a+1,5a-1,7a-5, 9a-11)             12(a-1).
                                                        (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4M)
```

Every last entry is positive in the stated range.  For `a=1,2,3`,
the five columns `delta=0,1,2,3,>=4` give the margin table

```text
a=1:       2, 4, 4, 6, 8,
a=2:      12, 9,13,15,18,
a=3:      18,14,18,20,24.                       (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N)
```

These are all positive.  Equations
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4L)--(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N)` exhaust the
arbitrary labels and prove the corollary.  QED.

The same argument closes the next factor count after an exact
classification of the low-mean boundary.

**Corollary 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECOND3F
(three-factor second radial base).**  Under the notation of Corollary
5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECOND2F, `K_(2,0)>=0` also holds for every
three-factor word, uniformly in the three labels.

**Proof.**  Sort the labels as `1<=a<=b<=c`, and put

```text
A_q=chi_q^2=sum_(t=0)^q beta_t,
D=A_aA_b=sum_t d_t beta_t,
E=DA_c=sum_t e_t beta_t,
S_c=sum_(t=0)^c d_t.
```

The boundary insertion identity gives

```text
e_0=S_c,
e_1=3S_c-2d_0-d_c+d_(c+1).                     (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4M0)
```

Hence `e_1/e_0>=5/2` is equivalent to

```text
Q_c=S_c-4d_0-2d_c+2d_(c+1)>=0.                 (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4M1)
```

First let `a=1`.  For `b>=2`, direct fusion gives

```text
D=(2,4,...,4,3,1),
```

where the string of fours occupies labels `1,...,b-1`.  At `c=b`,

```text
Q_b=4b-11,
```

which is nonnegative for `b>=3`.  At `c=b+1` it is `4b-8`,
and later it is still positive.  Thus the only cases not covered
here are `(a,b)=(1,1)` and `(a,b,c)=(1,2,2)`.

Next let `a=2`.  For every `b>=2`,

```text
d_0=3,       d_b=6,       d_(b+1)=3,
d_(b+2)=1,  sum_t d_t=9b+1.
```

Consequently

```text
Q_b=9b-21,           Q_(b+1)=9b-16,
```

and all later values are positive.  Only `(a,b,c)=(2,2,2)`
remains.

Finally suppose `a>=3`.  Formula
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4L)` gives

```text
d_0=a+1,               d_1>=3a,
d_2>=5a-4.
```

For `0<=k<=a`, the upper tail has the exact triangular form

```text
D_k:=d_(b+k)
  =(a-k+1)(a-k+2)/2.                            (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4M2)
```

Indeed a source `t` contributes to target `b+k` in exactly
`t-k+1` ways for `k<=t<=a`.  At `c=b`,

```text
Q_b=S_b-6(a+1)
    >=d_0+d_1+d_2-6(a+1)
    >=3a-9>=0.                                  (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4M3)
```

For `k>=1`, put `n=a-k+1` and
`T_r=r(r+1)/2`.  Since `D_k=T_n`,

```text
Q_(b+k)-Q_b
 =sum_(r=n+1)^a T_r+n(n-3)/2+2(a+1)>0.          (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4M4)
```

The possibly negative middle term is only `-1`, at `n=1,2`.
Beyond the support, deleting the final `-2d_c` can only increase
`Q_c`.  This proves `e_1/e_0>=5/2` in every nonexceptional case.
Since

```text
3(5/2)^2-4(5/2)-8=3/4>0,
```

Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECONDTHR proves `K_(2,0)>=0`
there.

It remains to evaluate the exceptions.  For `(a,b)=(1,1)`, direct
fusion gives the margins

```text
c=1,2,3,4,5,>=6:       21,37,32,42,58,64.
                                                        (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4M5)
```

The words `(1,2,2)` and `(2,2,2)` have margins `78` and `216`,
respectively.  Every exception is therefore positive, completing the
three-factor proof.  QED.

There is also an unbounded factor-count family below the threshold
which closes exactly.

**Corollary 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECONDFUND
(all-fundamental second radial payment).**  For every `m>=1`, if

```text
P=chi_1^m,
P^2=sum_(h=0)^m c_h beta_h,
```

then `K_(2,0)>=0`.

**Proof.**  The standard ballot-number decomposition of
`chi_1^(2m)` is

```text
c_h=(2h+1)/(m+h+1) binom(2m,m-h),       0<=h<=m.
                                                        (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N0)
```

In particular `c_0=Cat_m`.  Dividing the first four nontrivial
coefficients by `c_0` gives

```text
c_1/c_0=3m/(m+2),
c_2/c_0=5m(m-1)/{(m+2)(m+3)},
c_3/c_0=7m(m-1)(m-2)/{(m+2)(m+3)(m+4)},
c_4/c_0=9m(m-1)(m-2)(m-3)/
          {(m+2)(m+3)(m+4)(m+5)}.
```

Substitution and cancellation yield

```text
K_(2,0)
 =c_0^2
   {168m(m-1)(2m+1)}/
   {(m+2)^2(m+3)(m+4)(m+5)}>=0.          (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N1)
```

This proves the claim for every factor count without a cutoff.  QED.

The adjacent-drop estimate used below is not special to ballot numbers.
It is an exact consequence of being the square of a parity-pure
nonnegative character.

**Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECONDSQDROP
(parity-square adjacent-drop bound).**  Let

```text
P=sum_(i>=0)p_i chi_(epsilon+2i),       p_i>=0,
epsilon in {0,1},
P^2=sum_(r>=0)c_r beta_r,
```

with finite support and zero continuation.  Then, for every `r>=0`,

```text
c_r-c_(r+1)
 =sum_(i+j=r-epsilon)p_ip_j
   -2sum_(i>=0)p_ip_(i+r+1)
 <=c_0.                                      (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N2A)
```

In particular the estimate holds for the doubled profile of every
ordinary factor word.

**Proof.**  Clebsch--Gordan gives the exact coefficient formula

```text
c_r=sum_(i,j>=0)p_ip_j
  1_(|i-j|<=r<=i+j+epsilon).                  (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N2B)
```

At `r=0`, only `i=j` contributes, so

```text
c_0=sum_i p_i^2.                              (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N2C)
```

On subtracting the formula at `r+1`, a positive term occurs exactly
at the upper boundary `i+j+epsilon=r`, and a negative term occurs
exactly at the lower boundary `|i-j|=r+1`.  The latter boundary has
two orientations, proving the identity in
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N2A)`.  If `n=r-epsilon>=0`, Cauchy--Schwarz
gives

```text
sum_(i=0)^n p_ip_(n-i)
 <=sqrt{sum_(i=0)^n p_i^2 sum_(i=0)^n p_(n-i)^2}
 =sum_(i=0)^n p_i^2
 <=c_0.                                       (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N2D)
```

For `n<0` the sum is empty.  Dropping the nonpositive
off-diagonal term proves the result.  A product of irreducible
characters has fixed parity and nonnegative Clebsch--Gordan
coefficients, so the final assertion follows.  QED.

The ballot estimate is therefore an immediate special case.

**Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECONDBALDROP
(ballot adjacent-drop bound).**  Let

```text
d_h=(2h+1)/(m+h+1) binom(2m,m-h),       0<=h<=m,
```

with zero continuation.  Then

```text
d_b-d_(b+1)<=d_0,                       0<=b<=m. (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N2)
```

**Proof.**  The case `b=0` is immediate from `d_1>=0`.
Apply Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECONDSQDROP to
`P=chi_1^m`; its squared coefficients are exactly the displayed
ballot numbers.  QED.

The strict `cpp_int` verifier
`character_ring_iter/verify_su2_ballot_drop_bound.cpp` is an
independent arithmetic cross-check.  It reduces the positive-drop
range to `524` integer pairs, checks them exactly, and verifies the
positive shifted degree-ten polynomial for the complementary
unbounded range.  The proof no longer depends on that finite
separation.

**Corollary 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECOND1ARB
(fundamentals plus one arbitrary factor).**  For every `m>=0` and
every `b>=1`, if

```text
P=chi_1^m chi_b,
P^2=sum_(h>=0)c_h beta_h,
```

then `K_(2,0)>=0`.

**Proof.**  The case `b=1` is Corollary
5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECONDFUND, and `m<=2` is covered by the
one--three-factor bases.  Hence take `m>=3,b>=2`.  Let

```text
chi_1^(2m)=sum_h d_h beta_h,
S_b=sum_(h=0)^b d_h.
```

Insertion of `chi_b^2` gives

```text
c_0=S_b,
c_1=3S_b-D_b,
D_b=2d_0+d_b-d_(b+1).                          (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N7)
```

Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECONDBALDROP gives

```text
D_b<=3d_0.                                      (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N8)
```

Suppose first that `m>=5,b>=3`.  Put `x=m-5`.  The ballot ratios in
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N0)` give

```text
11S_b-60d_0
 >=11S_3-60d_0

 ={4d_0(29x^3+366x^2+1249x+426)}/
   {(m+2)(m+3)(m+4)}>=0.                        (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N9)
```

Together with `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N8)`, this yields
`20D_b<=11S_b`.  If `m>=7,b=2`, put `x=m-7`; similarly,

```text
11S_2-60d_0
 ={3d_0(13x^2+115x+70)}/
   {(m+2)(m+3)}>=0.                             (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N10)
```

The remaining threshold cases are finite identities.  For `m=3`,

```text
d=(5,9,5,1),
```

and `b=3` gives `(S_b,D_b)=(20,11)`; later `b` only improves the
ratio.  For `m=4`,

```text
d=(14,28,20,7,1),
```

and the cases `b=3,4,>=5` give

```text
(S_b,D_b)=(69,34),(70,29),(70,28).
```

Finally `(m,b)=(6,2)` gives

```text
(S_b,D_b)=(704,385),              20D_b=7700<7744=11S_b.
```

Thus every case considered so far satisfies

```text
c_1/c_0=3-D_b/S_b>=49/20.
```

Since

```text
3(49/20)^2-4(49/20)-8=83/400>0,
```

Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECONDTHR proves `K_(2,0)>=0`.

Only `(m,b)=(3,2),(4,2),(5,2)` remain.  Direct fusion gives their
respective exact margins

```text
365,                         3731,                 39340.
                                                        (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N11)
```

They are positive, completing the arbitrary-`m,b` proof.  QED.

The square-drop identity also supplies the missing uniform prefix
reserve once at least two nonfundamental factors are present.

**Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECONDLOWRES
(two-factor-root low-shell reserve).**  Let `R` be an ordinary
factor word with at least two factors, and write

```text
R^2=sum_(t>=0)e_t beta_t.
```

Unless `R=chi_1^2`,

```text
L(e):=-45e_0+12e_1+12e_2+57e_3+19e_4>=0.
                                                        (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N12)
```

**Proof.**  First suppose `R=chi_1^m` with `m>=3`.  Substitution of
the ballot ratios in `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N0)` gives

```text
L(e)/e_0
 ={(m-3)(621m^3+1917m^2+1602m+1800)}
   /{(m+2)(m+3)(m+4)(m+5)}>=0.                 (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N13)
```

Now suppose that `R=T chi_q`, where `T` is nonempty and `q>=2`.
Put `T^2=sum_t f_t beta_t`, and let

```text
ell=(-45,12,12,57,19).
```

Ordinary fusion gives

```text
L(f A_q)=sum_(t>=0)h_q(t)f_t,

h_q(t)=sum_(r=0)^4 ell_r
 max(0,min(q,t+r)-|t-r|+1).                    (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N14)
```

For `q=2`, the complete nonzero dual row is

```text
(h_2(0),...,h_2(6))
 =(-21,72,148,245,183,95,19).                  (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N15)
```

Formula `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4C)` gives `f_1>=f_0` for every
nonempty factor word.  Hence

```text
L(f A_2)>=-21f_0+72f_1>=51f_0>0.
```

For `q>=3`, every dual coefficient in
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N14)` is nonnegative.  Here is the complete
unbounded check.  For `t=0,1,2,3`, increasing `q` beyond three adds
only positive `ell_r`, and the respective values at `q=3` are

```text
36,160,248,300.
```

For `t>=4` and `q<t`, the sole negative weight `ell_0` is absent.
For `q>=t`, put `k=min(q-t,4)`.  Counting the truncated intervals
in `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N14)` gives, for `k=0,1,2,3,4`,

```text
h_q(t)=338,438,526,602,621.                     (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N16)
```

Thus `h_q(t)>=0` in every case, and `h_q(0)>0`.  Since `f_0>0`,
this proves `L(f A_q)>0` for `q>=3`.  The all-fundamental and
nonfundamental alternatives exhaust `R`, proving the lemma.  QED.

**Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECONDPREFIX
(second-radial deletion prefix).**  Let `R` be a factor word with
at least two factors, let `2<=a<=b`, and put

```text
Q=R chi_a,
Q^2=sum_(t>=0)d_t beta_t,
S_b=sum_(t=0)^b d_t.
```

Then either

```text
(R,a,b)=(chi_1^2,2,2),                          (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N17)
```

or

```text
19S_b>=102d_0.                                  (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N18)
```

**Proof.**  Write `R^2=sum_t e_t beta_t`, so
`Q^2=(sum_t e_t beta_t)A_a`.  The contribution of source `e_t` to
the prefix through `a` is

```text
N_a(t)=
 a+1+t(4a+1-3t)/2,                 0<=t<=a,

N_a(t)=(2a-t+1)(2a-t+2)/2,         a<t<=2a,
                                                        (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N19)
```

and is zero later.  Indeed, for `t,s<=a` the fusion interval
contributes

```text
2min(t,s)+1-max(0,t+s-a)
```

targets through `a`; summing over `0<=s<=a` gives the first line.
For `t>a`, the contributing counts are
`1,2,...,2a-t+1`, giving the second line.  Also

```text
d_0=sum_(t=0)^a e_t.                            (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N20)
```

Suppose `a>=3`.  Formula `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N19)` gives

```text
N_a(0)=a+1,             N_a(t)>=3a,  1<=t<=a.
```

The second inequality follows because the first line of
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N19)` is concave in `t`, equals `3a` at
`t=1`, and is at least `3a` at `t=a`.  Put
`E=sum_(t=1)^a e_t`.  Since `R` is nonempty,
`e_1>=e_0` by `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4C)`, so `E>=e_0`.  Therefore

```text
S_b>=S_a
 >=(a+1)e_0+3aE
 >={(4a+1)/2}(e_0+E)
 >=(13/2)d_0.                                  (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N21)
```

This is stronger than `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N18)`.

It remains to take `a=2`.  Directly from
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N19)`,

```text
d_0=e_0+e_1+e_2,
S_2=3e_0+6e_1+6e_2+3e_3+e_4.
```

Consequently

```text
19S_2-102d_0=L(e).                              (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N22)
```

Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECONDLOWRES proves the desired
inequality unless `R=chi_1^2`.  In that exceptional root,

```text
Q^2=(6,13,11,5,1).
```

If `b>=3`, then `S_b>=35` and `d_0=6`, so
`19S_b>=665>612=102d_0`.  Only `b=2` remains, which is precisely
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N17)`.  QED.

**Theorem 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECONDALL
(uniform second lower-radial payment).**  For every factor word

```text
P=product_(j=1)^m chi_(a_j),              a_j>=1,
P^2=sum_(h>=0)c_h beta_h,
```

one has

```text
K_(2,0)=c_0(c_2+c_3+c_4)-c_1c_3>=0.       (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N23)
```

Thus the `A=2,L=0` member of `(OCRD)` is closed for arbitrary factor
count and arbitrary labels.

**Proof.**  The cases with at most three factors are Corollaries
5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECOND2F and
5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECOND3F.  Words with at most one
nonfundamental factor are covered by Corollary
5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECOND1ARB.

It remains to take `m>=4` and at least two nonfundamental factors.
Sort the labels, let `b` be the largest nonfundamental label and `a`
the second largest, and write

```text
P=Q chi_b,                   Q=R chi_a.
```

The word `R` has `m-2>=2` factors.  Under the notation of Lemma
5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECONDPREFIX, insertion of the last factor
gives

```text
c_0=S_b,
c_1=3S_b-(2d_0+d_b-d_(b+1)).                  (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N24)
```

Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECONDSQDROP gives

```text
d_b-d_(b+1)<=d_0.
```

Outside `(R,a,b)=(chi_1^2,2,2)`, the deletion-prefix lemma therefore
yields

```text
c_1/c_0
 >=3-3d_0/S_b
 >=3-3(19/102)
 =83/34.                                       (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N25)
```

The exact threshold margin is

```text
3(83/34)^2-4(83/34)-8=131/1156>0.
```

Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECONDTHR now proves
`K_(2,0)>=0`.  The exceptional word is `[1,1,2,2]`; direct ordinary
fusion gives

```text
(c_0,c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4)=(30,72,76,52,24),
K_(2,0)=816>0.                                 (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N26)
```

This exhausts all factor words and proves the theorem.  QED.

The next antidiagonal also has a complete unbounded fundamental
strand.

**Corollary 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDFUND
(all-fundamental third radial payment).**  For every `m>=0`, let

```text
P=chi_1^m,                    P^2=sum_h c_h beta_h,
D_m=(m+2)(m+3)(m+4)(m+5)(m+6).
```

Then both strict `A=3` columns are nonnegative.  More precisely,

```text
K_(3,0)
 =c_0^2 {360m(m-1)(m-2)}/D_m^2
  {2m^5+37m^4+256m^3+803m^2+1062m+360},

K_(3,1)
 =c_0^2 {60m(m-1)}/D_m^2
  {26m^6+513m^5+3836m^4+13233m^3
    +19808m^2+8484m+720}.                      (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N27)
```

**Proof.**  Use the ballot ratios

```text
c_h/c_0
 =(2h+1)m(m-1)...(m-h+1)/
   {(m+2)(m+3)...(m+h+1)},             0<=h<=5,
```

with the falling product interpreted as zero when `h>m`.
Substitution in

```text
K_(3,0)=c_0(c_3+c_4+c_5)-c_1c_4,

K_(3,1)=c_0(c_4+c_5)+c_1c_2-c_2c_3
```

and clearing `D_m^2` gives the two factorizations in
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N27)`.  Every remaining polynomial
coefficient is positive, while the displayed falling factors cover
the zero small-`m` cases.  QED.

The same ballot structure closes an unbounded dominant-label chamber
with one arbitrary factor.

**Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDBIN
(ballot--boundary insertion formula).**  Put

```text
d_t=[beta_t]chi_1^(2m),
B_t=binom(2m,m-t),                         B_t=0 for t>m,
c_r=[beta_r](chi_1^(2m)chi_b^2).
```

Then `d_t=B_t-B_(t+1)`.  For every `r>=0` with `b>=2r`,

```text
c_r=B_0+2sum_(t=1)^r B_t
       -sum_(t=b-r+1)^(b+r+1)B_t.              (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N28)
```

**Proof.**  The coefficient of `d_t` after multiplication by
`A_b=chi_b^2` is

```text
n_(b,r)(t)
 =max(0,min(b,t+r)-|t-r|+1).
```

When `b>=2r`, its successive differences are

```text
n_(b,r)(0)=1,
n_(b,r)(t)-n_(b,r)(t-1)=
  2,     1<=t<=r,
  0,     r<t<=b-r,
 -1,     b-r<t<=b+r+1,
  0,     t>b+r+1.                              (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N29)
```

Here `n_(b,r)(b+r+1)=0`, so the final `-1` is included.
Summation by parts in

```text
c_r=sum_(t>=0)(B_t-B_(t+1))n_(b,r)(t)
```

gives `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N28)`.  QED.

**Corollary 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDDOM
(dominant one-arbitrary-factor third radial payment).**  Let

```text
P=chi_1^m chi_b,                         b>=m+5,
E_m=(m+1)(m+2)(m+3)(m+4)(m+5),
B_0=binom(2m,m).
```

Then both `A=3` columns are positive.  Explicitly,

```text
K_(3,0)
 ={B_0^2/E_m^2}
  {240m^8+3768m^7+23808m^6+81648m^5
   +179952m^4+281400m^3+287904m^2
   +149280m+28800},

K_(3,1)
 ={B_0^2/E_m^2}
  {520m^8+9172m^7+65144m^6+240520m^5
   +501224m^4+610276m^3+442264m^2
   +175680m+28800}.                            (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N30)
```

**Proof.**  For `0<=r<=5`, the hypothesis `b>=m+5` makes every
term in the final sum of `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N28)` vanish.  Hence

```text
c_r=B_0+2sum_(t=1)^r B_t,

B_t/B_0=
 {m(m-1)...(m-t+1)}/{(m+1)(m+2)...(m+t)}.
```

Substitute these six coefficients in the two formulas preceding
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N27)` and clear `E_m^2`.  Exact expansion
gives `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N30)`.  Every coefficient in both
numerators is positive.  QED.

The complementary fixed small labels admit an exact symbolic
certificate.

**Corollary 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDSMALL
(small one-arbitrary-factor third radial payment).**  For every
`m>=0` and every `2<=b<=15`, both `A=3` columns of

```text
P=chi_1^m chi_b
```

are nonnegative.

**Proof.**  Fix `b`, put `H=b+5`, and clear the common positive
denominator

```text
D_(m,b)=product_(j=2)^(H+1)(m+j)
```

from the ballot ratios through shell `H`.  The numerator representing
shell `t` is exactly

```text
(2t+1) product_(j=0)^(t-1)(m-j)
 product_(j=t+2)^(H+1)(m+j).                    (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N31)
```

For `0<=r<=5`, multiply these numerators by the exact fusion count

```text
max(0,min(b,t+r)-|t-r|+1),             0<=t<=b+r.
```

Substitution in the two `A=3` formulas produces an integer
polynomial over `D_(m,b)^2`.  The only nonnegative integer roots
which must be removed are one factor `m` from `(b,L)=(2,0)` and one
factor `m` from `(b,L)=(3,1)`.  The quotient data are

```text
b     degree K_(3,0) / least coefficient
      degree K_(3,1) / least coefficient

2       11 /    58320       12 /    126360
3       14 /   184320       13 /    399360
4       16 /   450000       16 /    975000
5       18 /   933120       18 /   2021760
6       20 /  1728720       20 /   3745560
7       22 /  2949120       22 /   6389760
8       24 /  4723920       24 /  10235160
9       26 /  7200000       26 /  15600000
10      28 / 10541520       28 /  22839960
11      30 / 14929920       30 /  32348160
12      32 / 20563920       32 /  44555160
13      34 / 27659520       34 /  59928960
14      36 / 36450000       36 /  78975000
15      38 / 47185920       38 / 102236160.      (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N32)
```

Every one of the `726` quotient coefficients is strictly positive.
The strict `cpp_int` certificate
`character_ring_iter/verify_su2_fundamental_one_arbitrary_third.cpp`
constructs `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N31)` symbolically, performs the
fusion sums and the two determinant expansions, checks every
synthetic-division remainder, and verifies all `726` coefficient
signs.  Thus this is a finite exact polynomial certificate for all
integer `m>=0`, not a bounded evaluation in `m`.  QED.

The zero-contraction column in the remaining diagonal strip follows
from a spectral endpoint threshold.

**Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDZEROTHR
(third zero-contraction spectral threshold).**  Suppose

```text
C=sum_(h>=0)c_h beta_h>=0                 on [-1,3],
c_0>0,                         lambda=c_1/c_0.
```

If

```text
lambda>=19/7,
```

then

```text
K_(3,0)=c_0(c_3+c_4+c_5)-c_1c_4>=0.
                                                        (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N33A)
```

**Proof.**  Under normalized `SO(3)` Haar measure put

```text
dnu=C(x)dmu/c_0.
```

This is a probability measure on `[-1,3]` and
`int x dnu=lambda`, so necessarily `lambda<=3`.  The character
recurrence gives

```text
beta_4(x)=x^4-3x^3+3x.
```

Consequently

```text
K_(3,0)/c_0^2
 =Cov_nu(x,beta_4(x))
 =int (x-lambda)^2 q_lambda(x)dnu,

q_lambda(x)
 ={beta_4(x)-beta_4(lambda)}/{x-lambda}

 =x^3+(lambda-3)x^2+(lambda^2-3lambda)x
   +lambda^3-3lambda^2+3.                       (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N33B)
```

The quotient is interpreted by continuity at `x=lambda`.  Put
`lambda_0=19/7`.  Then

```text
343q_(lambda_0)(x)
 =343x^3-98x^2-266x+307.                        (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N33C)
```

On `[-1,0]`, after the change `u=x+1`, three times the four
degree-three Bernstein coefficients of the polynomial in
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N33C)` are

```text
396,1355,1187,921.
```

On `[0,1]` they are

```text
921,655,291,858.
```

They are all positive.  On `[1,3]` its derivative is

```text
1029x^2-196x-266;
```

this is positive at one, and its derivative is positive thereafter.
The value at one is `286`, so `q_(lambda_0)>0` on the complete
spectral interval.

It remains to compare larger means.  If
`v=lambda-lambda_0>=0`, direct subtraction gives

```text
q_lambda(x)-q_(lambda_0)(x)
 =v R_lambda(x),

R_lambda(x)
 =x^2+(lambda+lambda_0-3)x
  +lambda^2+lambda lambda_0+lambda_0^2
  -3lambda-3lambda_0.                           (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N33D)
```

At the left spectral endpoint,

```text
R_lambda(-1)=(215+203v+49v^2)/49>0,

partial_x R_lambda(-1)=(3+7v)/7>0.              (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N33E)
```

Since `R_lambda` is convex in `x`, its derivative stays positive
for `x>=-1`.  Thus `R_lambda>0` on `[-1,3]`, and
`q_lambda>=q_(lambda_0)>0`.  The integrand in
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N33B)` is nonnegative, proving the lemma.
QED.

**Corollary 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDZERO1ARB
(uniform one-arbitrary-factor third zero-contraction payment).**
For every `m>=0` and every `b>=1`, if

```text
P=chi_1^m chi_b,
```

then `K_(3,0)>=0`.

**Proof.**  The all-fundamental case `b=1`, the fixed labels
`2<=b<=15`, and the dominant chamber `b>=m+5` are Corollaries
5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDFUND,
5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDSMALL, and
5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDDOM.  It remains to take
`16<=b<=m+4`.  The following mean argument proves the larger strip

```text
10<=b<=m+4.
```

In particular `m>=6`.  Under the notation of
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N7)`, put

```text
D_b=2d_0+d_b-d_(b+1).
```

Then

```text
lambda=c_1/c_0=3-D_b/S_b.                       (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N33F)
```

If `6<=m<=9`, then `b>m`, so the boundary ballot numbers vanish and
the telescoping sum gives

```text
S_b=sum_(t=0)^m d_t=binom(2m,m)=(m+1)d_0,
D_b=2d_0.
```

Therefore

```text
lambda=3-2/(m+1)>=19/7.                         (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N33G)
```

Now let `m>=10`.  For fixed `0<=t<=10`, the ballot ratio is

```text
d_t/d_0
 =(2t+1) product_(j=0)^(t-1)
        {(m-j)/(m+j+2)}.                        (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N33H)
```

Every factor on the right is nondecreasing in `m`.  At `m=10`,
the sum through shell ten is the complete telescoping sum and equals
`11d_0`.  Hence

```text
S_b>=S_10>=11d_0.
```

Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECONDSQDROP gives
`d_b-d_(b+1)<=d_0`, and therefore `D_b<=3d_0`.  Substitution in
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N33F)` yields

```text
lambda>=3-3/11=30/11>19/7.                      (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N33I)
```

Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDZEROTHR now proves
`K_(3,0)>=0` in the remaining strip.  This exhausts all `m,b`.
QED.

Corollaries 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDFUND,
5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDDOM, and
5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDSMALL, together with Corollary
5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDZERO1ARB, close the `K_(3,0)`
column throughout the complete one-arbitrary-factor strand.  The
second column has a universal mean-payment threshold.

**Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDONETHR
(third one-contraction mean-payment threshold).**  Suppose

```text
C=sum_(h>=0)c_h beta_h>=0                    on [-1,3],
c_0>0,                            lambda=c_1/c_0.
```

Put

```text
alpha=(2+2sqrt(10))/3.
```

If `lambda>=alpha`, then

```text
K_(3,1)=c_0(c_4+c_5)+c_1c_2-c_2c_3>=0.
                                                        (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N34)
```

**Proof.**  Under normalized `SO(3)` Haar measure put

```text
dnu=C(x)dmu/c_0.
```

Let

```text
g(x)=beta_2(x)=x^2-x-1,

h(x)=beta_3(x)-beta_1(x)=x^3-2x^2-2x+1.
```

Ordinary character multiplication gives

```text
beta_2(beta_3-beta_1)=beta_4+beta_5.
```

Consequently

```text
K_(3,1)/c_0^2=Cov_nu(g,h)
 ={1\over2}int int F(x,y)dnu(x)dnu(y),          (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N35)

F(x,y)
 =(g(x)-g(y))(h(x)-h(y))

 =(x-y)^2(x+y-1)
   (x^2+xy+y^2-2x-2y-2).                       (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N36)
```

The following two pointwise payments hold:

```text
F(x,y)+16(alpha-x)(alpha-y)>=0,
                         -1<=x,y<=alpha,        (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N37)

F(x,z)-8(alpha-x)(z-alpha)>=0,
                         -1<=x<=alpha<=z<=3.    (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N38)
```

Here is a finite exact certificate for these degree-five polynomial
inequalities.  Put

```text
xi=(2-sqrt(10))/3.
```

For `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N37)`, partition the lower square into

```text
[-1,2]^2,
[-1,xi] x [2,alpha],
[xi,2] x [2,alpha],
```

their transposes, and `[2,alpha]^2`.  For
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N38)`, partition at `xi` and `2` in the first
coordinate.  After the affine map of each nontrivial rectangle to
the unit square, the exact bidegree-`(5,5)` Bernstein data are

```text
form / rectangle                   root (+,0,-)   leaves / depth

(N37) [-1,2]^2                       (36,0,0)          1 / 0
(N37) [-1,xi] x [2,alpha]            (34,2,0)          1 / 0
(N37) [xi,2] x [2,alpha]             (33,2,1)          4 / 3
(N38) [-1,xi] x [alpha,3]            (34,2,0)          1 / 0
(N38) [xi,2] x [alpha,3]             (34,2,0)          1 / 0.
                                                        (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N39)
```

The one negative root coefficient in the third row becomes
nonnegative after three alternating midpoint de Casteljau
subdivisions; all four resulting leaves are nonnegative.  Every
entry lies in `Q(sqrt(10))`, and its sign is decided exactly by
squaring rational integers after separating the rational and
radical parts.  Thus `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N39)` is an exact
finite polynomial certificate, not a sample of either rectangle.

For completeness, the omitted top rectangles are elementary.  If
`2<=x,y<=3`, then

```text
x+y-1>=3,

x^2+xy+y^2-2x-2y-2>=2.
```

The second inequality follows because both partial derivatives are
positive there and the value at `(2,2)` is two.  Hence `F>=0` on
the top square.  If `2<=x<=alpha<=z<=3`, then, writing
`a=alpha-x,s=z-alpha`,

```text
F(x,z)>=6(z-x)^2=6(a+s)^2>=24as>=8as,
```

which proves the omitted part of `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N38)`.
This completes the pointwise certificate.

It remains to make the global payment.  Split the spectral interval
at `alpha` and put

```text
D=int_(x<alpha)(alpha-x)dnu(x),

S=int_(x>=alpha)(x-alpha)dnu(x).
```

The mean hypothesis gives

```text
S-D=lambda-alpha>=0.                           (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N40)
```

On the upper square, both factors after `(x-y)^2` in
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N36)` are nonnegative: the second one is
increasing in each variable there and at `(alpha,alpha)` equals

```text
3alpha^2-4alpha-2=10.
```

Thus the upper--upper load is nonnegative.  The lower--lower part
of one half the double integral in `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N35)` is
at least `-8D^2` by `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N37)`.  Both orientations
of the cross part contribute at least `8DS` by
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N38)`.  Therefore

```text
Cov_nu(g,h)>=-8D^2+8DS=8D(S-D)>=0.              (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N41)
```

Together with `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N35)`, this proves the lemma.
QED.

**Corollary 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDONE1ARB
(uniform one-arbitrary-factor third one-contraction payment).**
For every `m>=0` and every `b>=1`, if

```text
P=chi_1^m chi_b,
```

then `K_(3,1)>=0`.

**Proof.**  The all-fundamental case, the fixed labels `2<=b<=15`,
and the dominant chamber `b>=m+5` are Corollaries
5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDFUND,
5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDSMALL, and
5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDDOM.  It remains to take the diagonal
strip

```text
16<=b<=m+4.                                    (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N33)
```

In particular `m>=12`.  Continue the notation

```text
S_b=sum_(t=0)^b d_t,
D_b=2d_0+d_b-d_(b+1),
lambda=c_1/c_0=3-D_b/S_b.
```

If `12<=m<=15`, then `b>m`, so

```text
S_b=(m+1)d_0,                 D_b=2d_0,
lambda=3-2/(m+1)>=37/13.
```

Now suppose `m>=16`.  The ballot ratios in
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N33H)` are nondecreasing in `m`.  At `m=16`
the complete telescoping sum is `17d_0`; hence

```text
S_b>=S_16>=17d_0.
```

Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECONDSQDROP gives `D_b<=3d_0`,
and therefore

```text
lambda>=3-3/17=48/17.                          (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N42)
```

Also `37/13>48/17`, while

```text
48/17>alpha
```

because `110>34sqrt(10)`, equivalently
`110^2-10(34)^2=540>0`.  Thus every member of the remaining strip
satisfies the hypothesis of Lemma
5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDONETHR; here `C=P^2` is pointwise
nonnegative.  The lemma proves `K_(3,1)>=0`.  This exhausts all
`m,b`.  QED.

Corollaries 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDZERO1ARB and
5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDONE1ARB therefore close both strict
`A=3` columns throughout the complete one-arbitrary-factor strand.

The strict exact verifier
`character_ring_iter/verify_su2_third_one_contraction_mean_payment.cpp`
constructs the kernel and all five nontrivial rectangles in
`Q(sqrt(10))`, converts them to Bernstein form, performs the one
required three-level subdivision tree, and reproduces every count in
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N39)`.  It also reconstructs the eight
successive `chi_2^2` insertions in the countercontrol below.

The mean threshold is not by itself an arbitrary-factor theorem.  For
the genuine word `P=chi_2^8`, direct ordinary fusion gives

```text
(c_0,c_1)=(227475,625992),

(3c_1-2c_0)^2-40c_0^2=-44792028324<0.           (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N43)
```

Thus `c_1/c_0<alpha`; the later arbitrary-factor argument must still
use the cumulative current outside the mean chamber.

The repeated word in that countercontrol is covered independently by
the repeated-factor theorem.  The two spectral thresholds together
with all already closed structured chambers still do not exhaust the
mixed words.

**Proposition 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDMIXOBS
(mixed third-radial threshold obstruction).**  Put

```text
P=chi_1^6 chi_2 chi_3,                 P^2=sum_h c_h beta_h.
```

Then

```text
(c_0,c_1)=(5772,15248),

7c_1-19c_0=-2932<0,                              (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N43A)

(3c_1-2c_0)^2-40c_0^2=-162999360<0.              (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N43B)
```

Thus neither Lemma
5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDZEROTHR nor Lemma
5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADTHIRDONETHR applies.  The word is not
repeated, has two distinct nonfundamental labels, has eight factors,
and its root support is eleven.  Hence it lies outside the proved
repeated, one-arbitrary-factor, two-factor, and support-at-most-five
chambers.  Nevertheless its two third-radial columns are positive:

```text
K_(3,0)=24095496,                 K_(3,1)=64241860. (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N43C)
```

Consequently those chambers plus the mean thresholds cannot prove the
full `A=3` row.  A new mixed-word cumulative payment is already
necessary at this fixed antidiagonal.

**Proof.**  Eight successive exact ordinary interval transforms give
the displayed coefficients and radial values.  Substitution gives
the two threshold margins.  The fail-closed
`--replay-third-threshold-obstruction` mode of
`probe_su2_second_lower_radial_threshold.cpp` reconstructs the whole
profile with arbitrary-precision integers and checks all six displayed
integers.  Its transcript is
`certificates/su2_third_threshold_mixed_obstruction.log`.  QED.

For a factor word of root support `n>=2`, Theorem
5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADSECONDALL and Lemma
5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2RADFIRST remove the first two lower-wall
columns from `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S3BP)`.  The unresolved ordinary
band therefore has

```text
n(n-1)-2
```

columns, with no label or factor-count cutoff.

The strict `cpp_int` probe
`character_ring_iter/probe_su2_second_lower_radial_threshold.cpp`
independently constructs all profiles and checks the stated finite-factor
formulas.  Through labels twelve and eight factors it checks `125,969`
nondecreasing words and `930,240` insertion profiles.  All second
radial margins are nonnegative in that box; the spectral threshold
leaves `60` words uncovered, and all `594` one--three-factor,
exceptional one-arbitrary-factor, and
all-fundamental formula checks pass.  Both `A=3` columns also have
zero failures, and the exact all-fundamental factorizations
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N27)` are replayed through eight factors.
The `36` dominant-label words in the standard box independently
replay both factorizations in `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N30)`.
The probe also checks the
parity-square adjacent-drop consequence after every word and the
deletion-prefix certificate used above.  Among `125,455` applicable
words its sole uncovered deletion word is `[1,1,2,2]`, and the
minimum covered ratio is `102/19`, at `[1,1,1,2,2]`.  These counts
are bounded cross-checks only.  The unbounded proof is the centered
identity `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4K)`, the parity-square boundary
identity `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N2A)`, the dual low-shell calculation
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N12)--(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N16)`, and the
exact prefix count
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N19)--(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N25)`.
The separate strict symbolic verifier
`character_ring_iter/verify_su2_fundamental_one_arbitrary_third.cpp`
also checks the `19` exact Bernstein, comparison, and mean-threshold
constants in
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N33C)--(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4N33I)`.

The second radial cone is not preserved by blind squared-factor
insertion.  Indeed the arbitrary nonnegative profile

```text
d=(1,0,3)
```

becomes

```text
d chi_1^2=(1,4,6,3),
```

and hence has

```text
K_(2,0)=1(6+3)-4*3=-3.                          (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S4O)
```

The probe reproduces this exact countercontrol.  The profile `d` is
not asserted to be a factor profile; the calculation rules out only
an induction on the whole nonnegative cone.  A completion beyond the
spectral chamber must retain the actual factor orbit or another
load-bearing square invariant.

The strict off-diagonal condition cannot simply be closed to equality.
For the square root

```text
p=(0,4,2,3),
```

its square coefficient profile is log concave, but the diagonal
column `(A,L)=(2,1)` has `K_(2,1)=-6`.  This does not contradict
`(OCSP)`: the other `B_2` column pays it inside the positive diagonal
Gram determinant.

The extended strict C++ diagnostics independently check the two
forms of the reduction.  Across variable factor words in the boxes

```text
(maximum_q,length)=(8,3),(6,4),(5,5),(4,6),
```

all `2,451,120` fixed-contraction columns are nonnegative, although
`1,596` fixed-row sums and hundreds of thousands of individual
exterior products are negative.  The arbitrary-root diagnostic
checks `598,947` off-diagonal columns among `4,355` log-concave
square profiles in its `maximum_length=6, maximum_coefficient=4`
box, again without a failure.  It also reproduces the exact diagonal
value `-6`.  These counts are bounded evidence only; the telescoping
identities and displayed diagonal obstruction are exact.

Two further shortcuts fail before the live root cone is reached.
First, the single central spectral inequality is insufficient.  The
profile

```text
c=(1,2,3)
```

is positive and log concave and satisfies

```text
sum_h (-1)^h c_h=2>=0,
```

but at `(A,L)=(1,0)` one has

```text
K_(1,0)=1*(2+3)-2*3=-1.                         (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S5)
```

In fact

```text
sum_h c_h beta_h(x)=3x^2-x-2=(3x+2)(x-1),
```

which is negative for `-2/3<x<1`.  Hence the complete spectral-square
linkage cannot be replaced by its value at the central torus point.

Second, one cannot prove the squared current by first giving the
unsquared factor-word operator a positive star cone.  For the genuine
three-factor word

```text
P=beta_1^3=beta_0+3beta_1+2beta_2+beta_3,
```

the root profile `p=(1,3,2,1)` is log concave, but

```text
p_0 sum_(t=0)^2 p_t-p_1^2=1*(1+3+2)-9=-3.       (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3S6)
```

Thus even the anchored diagonal minor of `N_p` is negative.  The
square and its complete exterior/Cauchy--Binet aggregation are
load-bearing.  The extended variable-word C++ diagnostic reproduces
this value and finds both root adjacent-minor and root star-minor
failures; those bounded counts are route evidence only.

That last distinction is necessary.

**Proposition 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2ARB
(arbitrary-root obstruction).**  Put

```text
P=beta_0+2beta_1+2beta_2+beta_4.
```

Then

```text
P^2=sum_(t=0)^8 c_t beta_t,
c=(10,21,25,21,15,9,5,1,1),
```

and at `(R,S)=(1,8)`,

```text
c_0(c_7+c_8)-c_1c_8=10(1+1)-21=-1.             (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3T)
```

Thus `(OCSP)` is false for a general nonnegative ordinary character.
The torus half-profile of this `P` is

```text
h=(6,5,3,1,1),
```

which fails log concavity at `h_3^2<h_2h_4`.  Therefore this is not a
factor-word counterexample: the interval-convolution/log-concavity
constraint is load-bearing.

**Proof.**  Ordinary Clebsch--Gordan multiplication gives the displayed
square.  Its fusion interval for `(1,8)` is `[7,9]`, with zero
continuation at label nine, so the displayed current is exact.  QED.

The strict `cpp_int` diagnostic
`character_ring_iter/probe_su2_ordinary_arbitrary_root_current.cpp`
constructs arbitrary nonnegative `P`, its exact square, the coefficients
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3N)--(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3O)`, and the complete
triangle `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3Q)`.  In its
`maximum_length=6, maximum_coefficient=4` replay, all `953,124`
rank-two identities agree exactly; `197,835` individual `d_(a,b)` are
negative, and the first complete-current obstruction is
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3T)`.  The identity and displayed obstruction are
exact; the bounded counts are cross-checks only.

Nor can the global sum in either exact decomposition be replaced by an
outside-in separation suffix on the full log-concave cone.  In the
Cauchy--Binet decomposition of Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB, take

```text
h_0=2,                  h_(-1)=h_1=1,
R=1,                    S=2.
```

The suffix over intermediate pairs with `j-i>=3` consists of the pair
`(-1,2)` and equals `-2`.

For the exterior Gram decomposition put

```text
p_t=h_t-h_(t+1),              x^(R)=N_Rp,
Omega_R(i,j)=p_i x^(R)_j-p_j x^(R)_i.
```

Lagrange's identity gives

```text
c_0(N_c)_(R,S)-c_Rc_S
 =sum_(0<=i<j)Omega_R(i,j)Omega_S(i,j).          (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3U)
```

The symmetric log-concave half-profile

```text
h=(12,11,10,3),                 p=(1,1,7,3)
```

has, at `(R,S)=(1,2)`, the exact fixed-separation energies

```text
gap 1: 5199,       gap 2: 1696,
gap 3:  -40,       gap 4:   30.                 (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3V)
```

Thus the suffix with gap at least three is `-10`, although the complete
current is `6885`.  Both exact representations require a genuinely
global allocation; sorting their summands only by intermediate
separation is insufficient.

The same strict analyzer
`character_ring_iter/probe_su2_symmetric_log_concave_autocorrelation.cpp`
reproduces `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3U)--(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3V)`.
Its enlarged `maximum_length=10, maximum_coefficient=12` scan found
zero complete-current failures in `574,647` cases, but found `60`
exterior gap-suffix failures and `5,595,358` Cauchy--Binet gap-suffix
failures.  The displayed integers are exact counterexamples; the zero
count for the unsplit current is evidence only.

One more wall-free countercontrol shows why the square origin may not be
replaced by scalar current tests.

**Proposition 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPOCB2PSD
(spectral-square obstruction).**  The log-concave profile

```text
c=(4,10,12,11,10,9,8,7,2)
```

has all diagonal currents at least `4`, all far-support boundary currents
at least `16`, and every anchored two-by-two Schur determinant

```text
A(c)_(R,R)A(c)_(S,S)-A(c)_(R,S)^2
```

at least `32`.  Nevertheless

```text
A(c)_(1,7)=-2.                                  (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3W)
```

Moreover its half-label character polynomial is negative at the central
torus point:

```text
sum_(h=0)^8 (-1)^h c_h=-1.                      (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3X)
```

Hence `c` cannot be a character square `P^2`.  Log concavity, every
diagonal current, the far boundary, and every anchored Schur bound still
do not replace pointwise spectral positivity.

**Proof.**  Direct interval summation gives the three stated minima and
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3W)`.  At the torus point `theta=pi/2`,
`chi_(2h)(theta)=(-1)^h`, which gives
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB3X)`.  A character square is pointwise nonnegative,
so this profile is outside the square orbit.  QED.

The strict C++ reproducer
`character_ring_iter/probe_su2_log_concave_diagonal_completion.cpp`
checks every displayed integer.  Its bounded search is not used as a
proof of any positive assertion.

The full quadratic slope reserve is load-bearing.  Replacing `A(a)`
by the single endpoint term used in the proof of Lemma
5A8H28UIA2CGLCPDEC would require

```text
a_0a_(|R-S|)-a_Ra_S
 +Cross(a,b)_(R,S)+A(b)_(R,S)>=0.                (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB4)
```

This is false.  At `K=7`, for the factor word

```text
[3,1,3,3,2,4],
```

the exact profiles

```text
a=(1008693,659329,412087,245442,
   138564,73183,34293,9902),

b=(-436758,969402,2025478,2629858,
   2736734,2364376,1594432,562030)
```

give, at `(R,S)=(1,1)`,

```text
left side of (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB4)
 =-1080727842664.
```

The strict C++ analyzer
`character_ring_iter/probe_su2_affine_image_shells.cpp` constructs
these profiles directly from the triangular line convolution and
checks this integer.  Hence any proof of `(CSP)` must retain
coupling across the complete fusion interval; endpoint-only payment
is unavailable.

Coupling between distinct prefix rays is also load-bearing.  In the
notation of `(CSP)`, define the diagonal-ray truncation

```text
DR_(R,S)
 =A(b)_(R,S)
  +sum_j u_j Cross(c^(j),b)_(R,S)
  +sum_j u_j^2 A(c^(j))_(R,S).                  (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB4A)
```

Thus `DR` retains every individual ray square but discards the
nonnegative cross-ray reserve

```text
sum_(i<j)u_i u_j Cross(c^(i),c^(j))_(R,S).
```

**Proposition 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPDR
(central cross-ray obstruction).**  In the half-label even sector of
`SU(2)_22`, take the factor word

```text
[4,10,2,1,5,5,7,8].
```

Its proper affine suffix and central shell are respectively

```text
a=(3250512040,2443186446,1800486614,1299924647,
   918631973,634673142,427952066,280733011,
   177820677,106456002,55988374,17383006),

b=(-1841854677,1686786533,4769347253,7262041559,
   9051977637,10065095739,10271803391,9689839908,
   8384095372,6463327665,4073947829,1391260890).
                                                        (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB4B)
```

The profile `a` is decreasing and nonnegative.  Nevertheless, at the
strictly off-diagonal target `(R,S)=(1,2)`,

```text
DR_(1,2)=-12336084827213641714.                 (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB4C)
```

The omitted cross-ray reserve is

```text
12336086914119343797,
```

and the complete current is therefore

```text
A(a+b)_(1,2)=2086905702083>0.                   (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB4D)
```

Hence `(CSP)` cannot be reduced to independent payments on its
prefix rays, even away from the automatic diagonal Gram sector; the
full positive polarization between distinct rays must be retained.

**Proof.**  The exact triangular line convolution and outside-in
affine decomposition give `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB4B)`.  Taking
`u_j=a_j-a_(j+1)`, with zero continuation, and substituting in
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB4A)` gives
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB4C)`.  Adding the omitted polarization gives
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZB4D)`.  The fail-closed replay

```text
character_ring_iter/probe_su2_affine_image_shells \
  --replay-central-cross-ray
```

reconstructs both profiles from the factor word, verifies the
monotonicity of `a`, and checks all three displayed integers.  Its
transcript is
`certificates/su2_central_cross_ray_obstruction.log`.  QED.

Proper-tail monotonicity has an exact reduction to paired slopes of
the ordinary fusion square.  Let `p` be the unperiodized half-profile
and write

```text
m_t=[e_t]p^2,                       b_t=m_t-m_(t+1),
```

with zero continuation beyond the support.

**Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIMR (paired-slope reduction).**  For
`n>=1` and `0<=r<K`,

```text
D_n(r)-D_n(r+1)
 =sum_(j>=n){b_(jL+r)+b_((j+1)L-r-2)}.           (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZC)
```

**Proof.**  Substitute `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZW)` into
`D_n(r)-D_n(r+1)`.  The first affine image contributes

```text
m_(jL+r)-m_(jL+r+1)=b_(jL+r),
```

and the reflected image contributes

```text
m_((j+1)L-r-2)-m_((j+1)L-r-1)
 =b_((j+1)L-r-2).
```

Summing over `j>=n` proves the identity.  QED.

One might try to prove `(AIM)` term by term through the following
statement.

**False target 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIMPS (log-concave paired
slopes).**  If `p` is nonnegative and log concave with interval
support, require

```text
b_(jL+r)+b_((j+1)L-r-2)>=0
```

for every `K>=1`, `L=2K+2`, `j>=1`, and `0<=r<K`.
Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLC proves that every actual factor-word root has the
stated shape, and this target would make Lemma
5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIMR prove `(AIM)` term by term.  It is false even on
the actual factor-word orbit.

At `K=2`, take the all-`Q=1` word of length `57`.  Thus

```text
W_hat=tau_1^57,                    L=6.
```

For `j=1,r=0`, its two slopes are

```text
b_6
 =-387157488198605014960015208861841826244865307824488,

b_10
 = 385237793190685710001147375059495530565751049234010,
```

and hence

```text
b_6+b_10
 =-1919695007919304958867833802346295679114258590478<0.
                                                        (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZF)
```

The complete outer suffix nevertheless remains strictly decreasing:

```text
D_1=(5906262631195424856966887753223081407698325515285798,
     3625239505720587253076167891860940451512652054151306,
     1222222698526192310662733239404483715806940170858000).
                                                        (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZG)
```

Therefore the summation over all affine images in
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZC)` is load-bearing.  The surviving target is the
global inequality

```text
sum_(j>=n){b_(jL+r)+b_((j+1)L-r-2)}>=0,          n>=1, 0<=r<K,
                                                        (AIMGS)
```

not nonnegativity of its individual summands.

The global sum has an exact two-particle boundary form.  This exposes
both the positive credit and the negative load without affine-image
bookkeeping.

**Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIMST (sum--separation transport
reduction).**  Let

```text
p=sum_(a>=0)p_a e_a,                  m=p^2,
b_t=m_t-m_(t+1),

S_(n,r)={jL+r,(j+1)L-r-2:j>=n}.
```

Then

```text
b_t
 =sum_(a+b=t)p_ap_b
   -sum_(|a-b|=t+1)p_ap_b,                         (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZH)

D_n(r)-D_n(r+1)
 =sum_(a,b>=0)p_ap_b{
      1_(a+b in S_(n,r))
      -1_(|a-b|-1 in S_(n,r))}.                    (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZI)
```

Consequently `(AIMGS)` is exactly the assertion that the
sum-boundary credit in `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZI)` pays the
separation-boundary load.

**Proof.**  The ordinary `SU(2)` product `e_ae_b` contains `e_t`
exactly when

```text
|a-b|<=t<=a+b.
```

Taking the difference of the indicators at `t` and `t+1` gives a
positive boundary at `t=a+b` and a negative boundary at
`t=|a-b|-1`.  Summing with weight `p_ap_b` proves
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZH)`.  Sum this identity over the two residue rays
in `S_(n,r)` and use Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIMR to obtain
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZI)`.  QED.

This also closes every suffix beyond the separation width.

**Corollary 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIMFT (far-tail
monotonicity).**  If the interval support of `p` is `[A,B]` and

```text
nL+r>=B-A,
```

then

```text
D_n(r)>=D_n(r+1)>=0.
```

In particular, if `nL>=B-A`, the entire suffix `D_n` is nonnegative
and decreasing.

**Proof.**  The negative boundary in
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZH)` has

```text
|a-b|-1<=B-A-1.
```

Thus `b_t>=0` for every `t>=B-A`, so the ordinary square profile `m`
is nonincreasing from that index onward.  Both indices in every
summand

```text
m_(jL+r)-m_((j+1)L-r-1)
```

lie in this decreasing tail, proving `D_n(r)>=0`.  Equation
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZC)` or `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZI)` proves the adjacent
monotonicity.  QED.

In fact the entire proper-tail hierarchy reduces to its first member.
The reduction uses log concavity only to order the signs; it does not
assert the false termwise positivity in
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZF)`.

**Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIM1 (single-reserve
reduction).**  Suppose the ordinary square profile `m=p^2` is
nonnegative and log concave with interval support.  If

```text
D_1(0)>=D_1(1)>=...>=D_1(K)>=0,                 (AIM1)
```

then

```text
D_n(0)>=D_n(1)>=...>=D_n(K)>=0
```

for every `n>=1`.

**Proof.**  Fix `r`.  The `j`th coordinate contribution is

```text
c_j(r)
 =m_(jL+r)-m_(jL+L-r-1),                        (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZJ)
```

where the two arguments have fixed positive separation
`L-2r-1`.  For a log-concave interval sequence, the ratio

```text
m_t/m_(t+h)
```

is nondecreasing in `t` for every fixed `h>0`.  Hence the nonzero
sequence `c_j(r)` has at most one sign change, from negative to
positive.  Since `D_n(r)=sum_(j>=n)c_j(r)`, nonnegativity of
`D_1(r)` implies nonnegativity of every later suffix: deleting an
initial negative term increases the suffix, and after the sign change
only nonnegative terms remain.

For adjacent monotonicity, put `b_t=m_t-m_(t+1)`.  Log concavity makes
the ratios `m_(t+1)/m_t` nonincreasing, so the nonzero sequence `b_t`
also has at most one sign change, from negative to positive.  For
`r<K`, its arguments in

```text
D_n(r)-D_n(r+1)
 =sum_(j>=n){b_(jL+r)+b_(jL+L-r-2)}
```

occur in the strict order

```text
jL+r < jL+L-r-2 < (j+1)L+r.
```

Thus the displayed individual `b` terms are negative first and
positive later.  Grouping each consecutive pair preserves at most one
negative-to-positive sign change, even though the unique mixed pair
may have either sign.  Nonnegativity of the complete `n=1` sum,
which is exactly the adjacent margin in `(AIM1)`, therefore implies
nonnegativity of every later grouped suffix.  QED.

For an actual factor word, `m=p^2` is the ordinary profile of the
doubled word.  The wall-free version of Lemma
5A8H28UIA2CGLC therefore supplies the log-concavity hypothesis in
Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIM1.  Consequently all of `(AIM)` is reduced
to the one central outer reserve `(AIM1)`.  Together with `(CIP)`,
the remaining arbitrary-factor theorem is now the two-part
single-reserve payment

```text
D_1 decreasing and nonnegative,
A(D_1)+Cross(D_1,sigma_0)+A(sigma_0)>=0.         (SRP)
```

The first half of `(SRP)` has a closed one-factor recurrence.  It
shows exactly where a squared factor obtains the reserve that repairs
the non-invariance of the decreasing cone.

For a profile `v=(v_0,...,v_K)`, put

```text
(Bv)_r=v_r-v_(r+1),                 0<=r<K,
(Bv)_K=v_K,

(Cu)_r=sum_(s=r)^K u_s.
```

Thus `B=C^(-1)`, and `v` is decreasing and nonnegative exactly when
`Bv` is coefficientwise nonnegative.  For a reduced factor
`0<=q<=floor(K/2)`, put

```text
F_q=(N_q^(K))^2,                    T_q=BF_qC.
```

For an ordinary profile `m`, write `D_1(m)` for its first outer
affine suffix and

```text
u(m)=BD_1(m).
```

**Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIMGEN (single-reserve generator
identity).**  Let `m'=chi_q^2m`.  Then

```text
u_r(m')
 =sum_(s=0)^K (T_q)_(r,s)u_s(m)+rho_(q,r)(m),    (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZK)
```

where

```text
rho_(q,r)(m)
 =sum_(t=L-2q+r)^(L+2q-r-1)m_t,        0<=r<2q,

rho_(q,r)(m)=0,                        2q<=r<=K. (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZL)
```

In particular, the correction is an ordinary consecutive first-wall
block with positive unit coefficients.

**Proof.**  Let `Pi_K` denote affine folding from the ordinary
character ring to the level-`K` fusion ring.  It is a ring
homomorphism, so

```text
Pi_K(m')=F_qPi_K(m).
```

The central affine shell is

```text
sigma_0(m)_r=m_r-m_(L-r-1),
```

and Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIF gives

```text
D_1(m)=Pi_K(m)-sigma_0(m).
```

Consequently

```text
D_1(m')
 =F_qD_1(m)+F_qsigma_0(m)-sigma_0(m').           (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZM)
```

Apply `B` to the first term.  For the remaining bracket, expand

```text
chi_q^2=sum_(a=0)^(2q)chi_a
```

and use the ordinary and finite Clebsch--Gordan intervals.  Adjacent
rows cancel every interior label.  Since `2q<=K`, the two wall
windows do not overlap, and the uncancelled labels are exactly

```text
L-2q+r,...,L+2q-r-1
```

when `r<2q`; there is no uncancelled label when `r>=2q`.  Hence

```text
B{F_qsigma_0(m)-sigma_0(m')}=rho_q(m).
```

Substitution in `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZM)` proves
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZK)--(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZL)`.  QED.

The recurrence holds at every affine wall, not only the first.  Put

```text
u_n(m)=BD_n(m),

rho_(n;q,r)(m)
 =sum_(t=nL-2q+r)^(nL+2q-r-1)m_t,       r<2q,

rho_(n;q,r)(m)=0,                       r>=2q.    (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZW)
```

**Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIMGENA (all-wall generator
identity).**  For every `n>=1`,

```text
u_(n,r)(m chi_q^2)
 =sum_(s=0)^K(T_q)_(r,s)u_(n,s)(m)
   +rho_(n;q,r)(m).                              (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZX)
```

**Proof.**  Insert the affine-image definition of `D_n` from
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZX)` and expand
`chi_q^2=sum_(a=0)^(2q)chi_a`.  The ordinary Clebsch--Gordan intervals
translate each image by at most `2q<=K`.  Contributions strictly
outside the cutoff `nL` regroup into `F_qD_n(m)`.  Adjacent rows of
`B` cancel every translated interior label.  At the cutoff, the
uncancelled labels are exactly

```text
nL-2q+r,...,nL+2q-r-1
```

for `r<2q`, and none for `r>=2q`.  This is the calculation in Lemma
5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIMGEN translated from `L` to `nL`; no outer boundary
term remains because `m` has finite support.  This proves
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZX)`.  QED.

The central shell has a complementary recurrence with the same wall
block and the opposite sign.

**Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPGEN (coupled central-reserve
recurrence).**  Put

```text
a(m)=D_1(m),                  b(m)=sigma_0(m),
u(m)=Ba(m),
```

and let `m'=m chi_q^2`.  Then

```text
u(m')=T_qu(m)+rho_q(m),                         (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZX0)

b(m')=F_qb(m)-C rho_q(m).                       (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZX1)
```

In particular, the positive consecutive wall block inserted into the
proper-suffix slopes is removed, cumulatively, from the central
shell.

**Proof.**  The first identity is Lemma
5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIMGEN.  Since `a=Cu`, `T_q=BF_qC`, and `CB=I`,

```text
a(m')=Cu(m')=F_qa(m)+C rho_q(m).
```

Affine folding is a ring homomorphism, so, with
`d=a+b=Pi_K(m)`,

```text
a(m')+b(m')=Pi_K(m')=F_qPi_K(m)=F_q{a(m)+b(m)}.
```

Subtract the formula for `a(m')` to obtain
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZX1)`.  QED.

Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLPCIPGEN makes the remaining arbitrary-factor
mechanism explicit.  The already proved payment `(AIMGP)` keeps the
first component of `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZX0)--(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZX1)`
inside `u>=0`; the unresolved step is to show that the complete
quadratic reserve in `(CSP)` pays the simultaneous subtraction
`C rho_q(m)` from the central shell.

The matrix `T_q` is not nonnegative.  At `K=2,q=1`,

```text
(T_1)_(0,*)=(0,-2,-2),

u_0(m chi_1^2)
 =m_4+m_5+m_6+m_7-2u_1(m)-2u_2(m).              (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZN)
```

Thus the consecutive wall block is load-bearing.  The exact
arbitrary-factor shape target is now the following payment.

**Target 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIMGP (all-wall global
payment).**  For every doubled factor-word ordinary profile `m`,
every reduced next factor `q`, every `n>=1`, and every `0<=r<=K`,
prove

```text
rho_(n;q,r)(m)
 >=sum_(s=0)^K max(-(T_q)_(r,s),0)u_(n,s)(m).    (AIMGP)
```

Assuming `(AIMGP)`, factor induction from `m=e_0` proves
`u_n(m)>=0` simultaneously for every `n`: discard the nonnegative
entries of `T_q` in `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZX)` and use the target for its
negative entries.  Thus every `D_n` is decreasing and nonnegative,
which proves `(AIM)` directly.  The `n=1` specialization is the
single-reserve target above; Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIM1 shows that this
specialization would already suffice, but the all-wall family has the
closed generator recurrence.  Each local wall block pays the complete
outer suffix beyond that wall, rather than one affine image.

The exact C++ analyzer
`character_ring_iter/analyze_su2_aim1_generator.cpp` checks the
functional decomposition through half-level `30`.  All `1,388,680`
residual coefficients agree with the nonnegative interval in
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZL)`, while `30,872` entries of `T_q` are negative.
Its transcript is `certificates/su2_aim1_generator.log`.
The independent arbitrary-word audit
`character_ring_iter/probe_su2_aim1_generator_payment.cpp` verifies
`1,238,541` all-wall instances of `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZX)` exactly and
finds no failure of `(AIMGP)` after all positive `T_q` entries are
discarded.  A separate length-`100` stress adds `199,616` identities
and payments without a failure.  Its transcript is
`certificates/su2_aim1_generator_payment.log`.  These zero failures
are bounded evidence for `(AIMGP)`, not its proof.

There is an exact cumulative line form of the same target.  It removes
the finite fusion matrices from the word dependence and leaves only
the commuting triangular-convolution semigroup.

For fixed `q,r`, define the coefficient of the payment functional on
ordinary square profiles by

```text
eta_(q,r)(t)
 =1_(L-2q+r<=t<=L+2q-r-1)
  +sum_(s=0)^K min((T_q)_(r,s),0){
       1_(t in S_(1,s))-1_(t-1 in S_(1,s))},     (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZP)
```

where the first indicator is zero when `r>=2q`, and for `s=K`,

```text
S_(1,K)={jL+K:j>=1}.
```

Thus `(AIMGP)` is

```text
sum_(t>=0)eta_(q,r)(t)m_t>=0.                    (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZQ)
```

These definitions display the `n=1` member.  The all-wall member is
obtained by replacing `L` with `nL` in the finite indicator and
`S_(1,s)` with `S_(n,s)`; the following calculation is unchanged.

Define the symmetric line functional

```text
kappa_(q,r)(0)=2eta_(q,r)(0),

kappa_(q,r)(x)
 =eta_(q,r)(|x|)-eta_(q,r)(|x|-1),       x!=0.  (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZR)
```

**Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIMCL (cumulative line
reduction).**  If `W_hat` is symmetric and

```text
m_t=W_hat(t)-W_hat(t+1),                 t>=0,
```

then

```text
2sum_(t>=0)eta_(q,r)(t)m_t
 =sum_(x in Z)kappa_(q,r)(x)W_hat(x)
 =(kappa_(q,r)*W_hat)(0).                        (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZS)
```

Consequently `(AIMGP)` for an arbitrary factor word is exactly

```text
(kappa_(q,r)*product_j tau_(q_j))(0)>=0          (AIMCL)
```

for every finite multiset `q_j in {1,...,floor(K/2)}` and every
admissible proposed next factor `q` and row `r`.

**Proof.**  Substitute `m_t=W_hat(t)-W_hat(t+1)` in
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZQ)` and shift the second sum by one.  The coefficient
of `W_hat(0)` is `eta_(q,r)(0)`, while that of `W_hat(x)` for `x>0`
is

```text
eta_(q,r)(x)-eta_(q,r)(x-1).
```

Symmetry of `W_hat` splits this coefficient equally between `x` and
`-x`, giving `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZR)--(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZS)`.
Finally insert `W_hat=product_j tau_(q_j)`.  QED.

The functional `kappa_(q,r)` is an eventually `L`-periodic symmetric
integer sequence with one finite first-wall defect.  Thus `(AIMCL)`
is a pure cumulative random-walk statement: the complete convolution
product must pay the defect at the origin.  It no longer asks for
positivity of any individual affine image or individual factor.

This statement has a finite spectral/local split.  Let
`bar_kappa_(q,r)` be the unique `L`-periodic sequence which agrees
with `kappa_(q,r)` outside its finite first-wall transient, and put

```text
e_(q,r)=kappa_(q,r)-bar_kappa_(q,r).
```

The sequence `e_(q,r)` has finite support.  For
`zeta_l=exp(2pi i l/L)`, use the cyclic Fourier transform

```text
hat_kappa_(q,r)(l)
 =sum_(a=0)^(L-1)bar_kappa_(q,r)(a)zeta_l^(-a).
```

**Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIMSL (spectral/local reserve
split).**  For `W_hat=product_j tau_(q_j)`,

```text
2sum_(t>=0)eta_(q,r)(t)m_t
 =1/L sum_(l=0)^(L-1) hat_kappa_(q,r)(l)
       product_j beta_(q_j)(zeta_l)^2
  +sum_(x in Z)e_(q,r)(x)W_hat(x).                (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZT)
```

Every word-dependent factor in the finite spectral sum is
nonnegative.

**Proof.**  Split `kappa=bar_kappa+e` in
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZS)`.  Pairing the periodic part with the finite
sequence `W_hat` is the same as pairing `bar_kappa` with the cyclic
periodization of `W_hat`.  Fourier inversion on `Z/LZ` gives the
first term in `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZT)`.  Since

```text
hat_W(l)=product_j tau_(q_j)(zeta_l)
        =product_j beta_(q_j)(zeta_l)^2,
```

these factors are real and nonnegative.  The finite defect gives the
last term.  QED.

Neither term in `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZT)` is separately nonnegative.  At
`K=2,q=1,r=0`, the periodic line functional and the spectrum of
`tau_1` are respectively

```text
bar_kappa=(0,-2,2,0,2,-2),

hat_bar_kappa=(0,-4,0,8,0,-4),
hat_tau_1=(9,4,0,1,0,4).                         (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZU)
```

Thus on an all-`Q=1` word of length `N`, the periodic term is

```text
{8-8*4^N}/6<0,                         N>=1.     (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZV)
```

The finite defect term is therefore load-bearing for every
nontrivial length.  Formula `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZT)` isolates the live
uniform problem sharply: prove that the local coefficients of the
triangular product pay the explicitly negative cyclic modes for every
multiset of factors.

The factor-word hypothesis in `(AIMGP)` cannot be replaced by log
concavity plus an already nonnegative reserve.  At `K=3,q=1,r=0`,
put

```text
m=(32,64,128,256,384,576,864,1296,
   1944,1944,1944,972,486,243).
```

Its successive ratios are

```text
2,2,2,3/2,3/2,3/2,3/2,3/2,1,1,1/2,1/2,1/2,
```

so `m` is positive and log concave.  Direct evaluation gives

```text
u(m)=(0,243,1215,486),              (T_1)_(0,*)=(0,-2,-3,-4),

rho_(1,0)(m)=m_6+m_7+m_8+m_9=6048,

2u_1+3u_2+4u_3=6075.                             (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZO)
```

Thus the abstract payment margin is `-27`, despite `u(m)>=0`.
The strict adaptive-thread C++ reproducer
`character_ring_iter/probe_su2_aim1_abstract_payment.cpp` finds this
exact witness and records it in
`certificates/su2_aim1_abstract_payment.log`.  Consequently a proof
of `(AIMGP)` must use the triangular-convolution factor-word origin,
not only the two scalar shape hypotheses.

Normalized-dimension monotonicity and the old reserve are likewise
insufficient without log concavity.  At `K=5,q=1,r=0`, put

```text
m=(19,54,85,119,153,176,195,210,221,228,
   252,276,300,297,290,279,132,105,74).
```

Then

```text
m_t/(2t+1)
 =(19,18,17,17,17,16,15,14,13,12,
   12,12,12,11,10,9,4,3,2)
```

is decreasing, and direct evaluation gives

```text
u(m)=(3,7,11,147,101,31),
(T_1)_(0,*)=(0,-2,-3,-4,-4,-4).
```

The consecutive wall block is `1125`, while the negative transform
load is `1163`, so the payment margin is `-38`.  This profile is not
log concave.  Together with `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZO)`, this isolates the
following strictly sharper abstract route.

**False target 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIM3 (three-condition wall
payment).**  Let `m` be a nonnegative finite interval profile such
that

```text
m_t^2>=m_(t-1)m_(t+1),
(2t+3)m_t>=(2t+1)m_(t+1),                       (AIM3S)
```

at every applicable index.  If `u_n(m)>=0` coordinatewise at an
affine wall `nL`, prove, for every reduced `q` and every row `r`,

```text
rho_(n;q,r)(m)
 >=sum_s max(-(T_q)_(r,s),0)u_(n,s)(m).          (AIM3)
```

The implication is false, even uniformly in the level.

**Proposition 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIM3X (three-condition
obstruction).**  For every `K>=3`, put `L=2K+2` and

```text
m_t=min(t+1,L),              0<=t<=L+K,
m_t=0,                       t>L+K.              (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZO0)
```

Then `m` is log concave and normalized-dimension decreasing, and

```text
u_1(m)=(0,...,0,L).
```

Nevertheless, for `q=1,r=0`, the payment margin in `(AIM3)` is
exactly `-1`.

**Proof.**  Before the plateau, the successive ratios are
`2,3/2,4/3,...,L/(L-1)`; they then equal `1` until the terminal
zero.  Hence they are nonincreasing and `m` is log concave.  For
`t<L`,

```text
(2t+3)(t+1)-(2t+1)(t+2)=1,
```

while normalized-dimension monotonicity is immediate on the plateau
and at the terminal zero.

Write `b_t=m_t-m_(t+1)`.  Every slope selected by `u_(1,s)` vanishes
except

```text
b_(L+K)=L,
```

which belongs to the middle coordinate `s=K`.  Thus the displayed
reserve vector follows.  Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIMW gives

```text
max(-(T_1)_(0,K),0)=4,                    K>=3.
```

The first-wall block is

```text
rho_(1;1,0)=m_(L-2)+m_(L-1)+m_L+m_(L+1)=4L-1.
```

Therefore its payment margin is `(4L-1)-4L=-1`.  QED.

The earlier random-ratio audit found no failure in `29,315,849`
three-condition payments because its bounded generator did not reach
this plateau-and-cutoff family.  The exhaustive strict C++ analyzer
`character_ring_iter/analyze_su2_aim3_exhaustive.cpp` independently
finds the first `K=3` instance

```text
m=(1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,8,8,8,8),
u=(0,0,0,8),
rho=31,                                  payment=31-4(8)=-1.
```

It records `1,108` exact payment failures in its bounded box.
Consequently log concavity, normalized-dimension monotonicity, and an
already nonnegative reserve do not close `(AIMGP)`.  Any proof must
retain a stronger invariant of the triangular-convolution
factor-word origin.

The smallest surviving strengthening is to retain the ordinary
character square itself.

**Target 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIMSRP (log-concave-square-root
payment).**  Let `p` be a nonnegative finite log-concave interval
profile, put `m=p^2` in the ordinary `SU(2)` character ring, and
assume `u_n(m)>=0`.  Prove, for every reduced next factor `q` and
every row `r`,

```text
rho_(n;q,r)(m)
 >=sum_s max(-(T_q)_(r,s),0)u_(n,s)(m).          (AIMSRP)
```

This target retains exactly the structure discarded by the
counterexample `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZO0)`.  Every ordinary half-profile
of a factor word is log concave by Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLC, and its
doubled profile is its ordinary character square.  Hence `(AIMSRP)`
would imply `(AIMGP)` and close the all-wall reserve induction.

The exhaustive log-concave-root analyzer
`character_ring_iter/probe_su2_aim_log_concave_roots.cpp` checks
`2,541,825` exact instances of `(AIMSRP)` for all roots through index
eight with coefficients at most six and all half-levels through ten,
without a failure.  The independent structured-family stress
`character_ring_iter/probe_su2_aim_square_root_families.cpp` extends
constant intervals, linear ramps, tents, trapezoids, binomial rows,
and powers through support length `120` and half-level `60`.  Every
one of its `1,185,555` proper suffixes has nonnegative reserve, and
all `332,416,738` exact payments pass.  These are complementary
bounded data for the square-root target, not its proof.

There is now a sharper exact reduction of `(AIMSRP)`.  For fixed
`K,n,q,r`, let `Lambda_(n;q,r)` denote its payment functional:

```text
Lambda_(n;q,r)(m)
 =rho_(n;q,r)(m)
  -sum_s max(-(T_q)_(r,s),0)u_(n,s)(m).
```

For two ordinary profiles `p,z`, define the symmetric bilinear form

```text
mathcal B_(n;q,r)(p,z)
 =Lambda_(n;q,r)(pz).                            (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZO0A)
```

Here `pz` is ordinary `SU(2)` character multiplication.

**Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIMLC (nested-layer
reduction).**  Suppose

```text
mathcal B_(n;q,r)(1_I,1_J)>=0                    (AIMNI)
```

for every pair of finite integer intervals `I,J` such that `I`
contains `J` or `J` contains `I`.  Then

```text
Lambda_(n;q,r)(p^2)>=0
```

for every nonnegative finite unimodal profile `p`.  In particular,
`(AIMNI)` implies `(AIMSRP)`.

**Proof.**  The nonempty superlevel sets of a finite unimodal profile
are finite nested intervals.  Ordering its distinct positive levels
gives an exact finite decomposition

```text
p=sum_i c_i 1_(I_i),                c_i>0,
I_1 subseteq I_2 subseteq ... .
```

By bilinearity,

```text
Lambda(p^2)
 =sum_(i,j)c_ic_j mathcal B(1_(I_i),1_(I_j))>=0.
```

Every log-concave interval profile is unimodal, proving the final
claim.  QED.

Thus the live analytic statement is the interval inequality
`(AIMNI)`, not a nonlinear inequality on arbitrary roots.  It has an
explicit two-dimensional kernel.  Put

```text
E_(n;q,r)(v)=sum_(t=0)^v eta_(n;q,r)(t),
```

with `E(v)=0` for `v<0`, where `eta_(n;q,r)` is the all-wall version
of `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZP)`.  The ordinary Clebsch--Gordan interval gives

```text
mathcal B_(n;q,r)(e_a,e_b)
 =E_(n;q,r)(a+b)-E_(n;q,r)(|a-b|-1).             (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZO0B)
```

The period potential has a uniform one-dimensional positivity
structure.  Put

```text
P(x)=sum_(v=x)^(x+L-1)E(v),             E(v)=0 for v<0.
```

**Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIMPP (period-potential
positivity).**  For every `K,n,q,r`,

```text
E(v)>=0,                                             (AIMPP1)
E(v+L)>=E(v),                                        (AIMPP2)

sum_(v=0)^(x-1)E(v)+sum_(v=0)^(L-x-2)E(v)
 <=P(0),                                  0<=x<L.   (AIMPP3)
```

Empty sums are zero.  Hence `P` is nondecreasing.

**Proof.**  The result is trivial for `r>=2q`; assume `r<2q` and put
`a=2q-r`.  Use Lemma 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIMW to write the payment as

```text
Lambda(m)=rho(m)-sum_s b_sD_n(s).
```

Therefore its coefficient sequence is

```text
eta(t)
 =1_(nL-a<=t<=nL+a-1)
  -sum_s b_s sum_(j>=n){
       1_(t=jL+s)-1_(t=(j+1)L-s-1)}.              (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZO0C)
```

Let `B(y)=sum_(s<=y)b_s`.  The explicit stable weights in
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZO2)` give

```text
B(y)<=a+y+1,                         0<=y<a,
B(y)<=2a,                            y>=0.         (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZO0D)
```

Indeed, when `r<q`, the only nonzero prefix below `a` is
`B(y)<=2(y-r)`, and the first displayed bound follows from
`y<=2q+r+1`.  When `q<=r<2q`, the stable support starts at
`3r-2q+2>a`, so that prefix is zero.  The total stable weight is
`2a` in both cases, and `0<=b<=bar b`.

Now sum `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZO0C)`.  Before the wall, `E` is zero and
then rises by one across the left half of the boundary block.  On the
right half it is respectively

```text
a+y+1-B(y),                         0<=y<a,
2a-B(y),                            a<=y<=K,
2a-B(L-y-2),                        K<y<L,
```

where `y` is the residue after the wall.  Later periods repeat the
last two forms, with baseline `2a`.  Bounds
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZO0D)` prove `(AIMPP1)`.  Comparing one period apart
leaves either zero, a boundary ramp, `a-y-1` for `0<=y<a`, or

```text
2a-B(a-k-2)-(k+1)>=0
```

on the reflected left ramp; the first bound in
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZO0D)` proves the last inequality.  This gives
`(AIMPP2)`.

For `n>=2`, `E` vanishes throughout the first period, so `(AIMPP3)`
is immediate.  For `n=1`, its first-period values are zero through
`L-a-1` and then `1,2,...,a`.  Since `a<=K<(L-1)/2`, at most one of
the two prefixes in `(AIMPP3)` reaches that terminal ramp, and that
prefix is bounded by its complete sum `P(0)`.  QED.

**Corollary 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIMPB (positive period
blocks).**  If `J` is any interval of exactly `L` consecutive
indices, then

```text
mathcal B_(n;q,r)(e_a,1_J)>=0
```

for every `a>=0`.

**Proof.**  Write `J=[c,c+L-1]`.  If `a<c`, summing
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZO0B)` gives

```text
P(a+c)-P(c-a-1)>=0.
```

If `a>c+L-1`, it gives

```text
P(a+c)-P(a-c-L)>=0.
```

Both follow from monotonicity of `P`.  If `a=c+x` lies in `J`, the
separation term is

```text
sum_(v=0)^(x-1)E(v)+sum_(v=0)^(L-x-2)E(v),
```

whereas the sum term is `P(a+c)>=P(0)`.  Apply `(AIMPP3)`.  QED.

By bilinearity, every full period block can therefore be removed from
either interval in `(AIMNI)` at nonnegative cost.  In a nested pair,
one may reduce the inner width below `L` and both outer extensions
below `L`.  Together with eventual period translation of `E`, this
reduces the remaining proof of `(AIMNI)` to short nested rectangles
near the first active wall.  The reduction is exact; the still-open
step is a uniform proof of those short rectangles as `K,q,r` vary.

The short nested rectangle separates without cancellation.  If
`J subseteq I`, write

```text
I=I_- disjoint_union J disjoint_union I_+,
```

where `I_-` and `I_+` may be empty and are contiguous with `J`.
Then

```text
mathcal B(1_I,1_J)
 =mathcal B(1_J,1_J)
  +mathcal B(1_(I_-),1_J)
  +mathcal B(1_(I_+),1_J).                       (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZO0E)
```

Thus `(AIMNI)` follows from the two sharper statements

```text
mathcal B(1_J,1_J)>=0,                           (AIMNIS)

mathcal B(1_U,1_V)>=0                            (AIMNIA)
```

whenever `U,V` are adjacent disjoint intervals (so `U union V` is an
interval).  Symmetry handles
the two possible orders in `(AIMNIA)`.  The optimized audit finds no
negative interval core, no negative best left or right contiguous
extension, and no negative one-sided sum.  Hence the remaining
uniform problem is interval self-payment `(AIMNIS)` and contiguous
interval payment `(AIMNIA)`; neither is yet proved for unbounded
`K,q,r`.

In fact `(AIMNIA)` implies `(AIMNIS)`.  Split a nonsingleton interval
`J=J_1 disjoint_union J_2` into adjacent nonempty intervals.  Then

```text
mathcal B(1_J,1_J)
 =mathcal B(1_(J_1),1_(J_1))
  +mathcal B(1_(J_2),1_(J_2))
  +2mathcal B(1_(J_1),1_(J_2)).
```

Induction on the width and the singleton identity

```text
mathcal B(e_a,e_a)=E(2a)>=0
```

prove `(AIMNIS)`.  Thus adjacent intervals are the only live case.

They have a one-dimensional form.  Put

```text
S_l(x)=sum_(v=x)^(x+l-1)E(v),
Theta_(l,w)(z)=sum_(x=0)^(w-1)S_l(z+x).
```

For adjacent intervals

```text
U=[A,C-1],              V=[C,C+w-1],
l=C-A,                  z=A+C=2A+l,
```

direct summation of `(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZO0B)` gives

```text
mathcal B(1_U,1_V)
 =Theta_(l,w)(z)-Theta_(l,w)(0).                 (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZO0F)
```

Consequently the remaining global-payment statement is

```text
Theta_(l,w)(z)>=Theta_(l,w)(0),
l,w>=1, z>=l, z=l (mod 2).                       (AIMPT)
```

Corollary 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIMPB removes full `L`-blocks from either
adjacent interval at nonnegative cost, so it is enough to take
`1<=l,w<L`.  Inequality `(AIMPP2)` then reduces `z` to
`l<=z<l+L` with the same parity.  Finally, when `n>=3`, every
potential value entering `Theta_(l,w)(0)` is before the active wall
and hence zero.  Since `E>=0`, `(AIMPT)` is automatic.  The sole
remaining analytic range is therefore

```text
n in {1,2}, 1<=l,w<L, l<=z<l+L, z=l (mod 2).     (AIMPTF)
```

This is finite at each level but still requires a uniform
piecewise proof as `K,q,r` grow.

There is a stronger reduction which removes `q,r` from the analytic
part altogether.  Put

```text
I_d(X)=1+X+...+X^(d-1)
```

and, for an `(AIMPTF)` row, define the three-box profile

```text
g_h=[X^(h-1)]I_l(X)I_w(X)I_z(X),        g_h=0 outside its support.
                                                        (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZO0G)
```

Indeed, if

```text
tau(t)=[X^t]I_l(X)I_w(X),
```

then

```text
E(z+t)-E(t)=sum_(h=t+1)^(t+z)eta(h).
```

Multiplying by `tau(t)` and summing gives the exact crossing
identity

```text
Theta_(l,w)(z)-Theta_(l,w)(0)
 =sum_(h>=0)eta(h)g_h
 =Lambda_(n;q,r)(g).                         (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZO0H)
```

Thus the trapezoidal shift is the original payment functional
evaluated on the coefficient sequence of three interval
polynomials.  The parity condition has become the central nesting

```text
z=l+2A,                         0<=A<=K.          (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZO0I)
```

For any finite profile `g`, put

```text
D_n^g(s)
 =sum_(j>=n){g_(jL+s)-g_((j+1)L-s-1)}.           (P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZO0J)
```

The surviving three-box statement is the following pair of
labelwise inequalities.

**Target 5A8H28UIA2CGLCPAIMTBF (three-box affine
folding).**  Let `L=2K+2`, `n in {1,2}`, `1<=l,w<L`, and
`z=l+2A` with `0<=A<=K`.  For the profile in
`(P5A.102AD5ALX1ZZO0G)`, prove

