edges in this matching, `(P23.11z5zy7s6)` therefore gives

```text
N>=wr_M.
```

The three perfect matchings partition the colored edges.  Hence one has
`r_M>=ceil(c/3)`, and for `7<=c<=12`,

```text
N>=3ceil(c/3)>=c=T_nt.
```

This proves `(P23.11z5zy7s3)`.

Now suppose `x_2=Jx_1`.  The matching
`{1,2}|{3,4}` has no active colored edge: the first fusion interval is
the singleton `{J}`, while activity on the opposite edge would require
`Ja=J` or `Jq=J`, forcing a trivial minus label.  Thus every active edge
crosses this matching.  For example, a `q`-colored edge `{1,3}` gives

```text
q in x_1 star_k x_3,
Ja in x_2 star_k x_4=J(x_1 star_k x_4),
```

and hence `a in x_1 star_k x_4`.  Pairing both relations through the
common channel `x_1` proves

```text
m(q,a,x_3,x_4)>=1.
```

The other three crossing edges, and the other color, give the same
conclusion after using the common channel `x_1` or `x_2`.  Finally

```text
m(J,x_1,Jx_1)=1,
```

so the indexed pair `{x_3,x_4}` in the two-plus sum defining `U_2`
has the positive product `(P23.11z5zy7s4)`.  This proves the supplier
claim.  Combining it with the generic closure proves the residual
statement `(P23.11z5zy7s5)`.  QED.

The first collision-column margin is already cap-localized.

**Lemma 23A9S2D1 (lone-`J` eight-edge plus-cap localization).**  Retain the
setting of Lemma 23A9S2D, suppose

```text
c=T_nt=8,
```

and assume `T_nt>N+P_eq`.  Then all four labels `x_i` have cap at most
three.

**Proof.**  Suppose one label, say `z=x_1`, has cap at least four.
It has colored degree at least two, since otherwise its one edge and the
at most six colored edges on the other three vertices would give
`c<=7`.

Choose an incident edge of color `r`, and write `s` for the other minus
label.  Its active triple `A` is nonminimal by Lemma 23A9S2B2.  Its
four-label complement contains `J`; canceling the simple current gives
the positive invariant triple

```text
C={Js,x_u,x_v}
```

on the two vertices outside the edge.  Both `A` and `C` have profile at
least `(1,2,1)`.  If `C` were also nonminimal, Lemma 23A9S2B2 and
orthogonality would give `N>=8`.  The strict deficit with `T_nt=8`
therefore forces `C` to be minimal.  Consequently

```text
s in {2,k-2},                    x_u,x_v in {1,k-1}. (P23.11z5zy7s9)
```

Apply this to two distinct edges at `z`.  All three other `x`-labels
have cap two.  Both minus labels have cap three as well.  Indeed, if
only one minus label had cap three, all edges at `z` would have the
other color, while edges avoiding `z` could only have the cap-three
color.  The two color classes would then contain at most `3+3=6`
edges.

Thus the minus labels lie in `{2,k-2}`.  Fusing `z` with a label of cap
two to one of these two outputs, and using `cap_k(z)>=4`, forces

```text
z in {3,k-3}.                                      (P23.11z5zy7s10)
```

Assume first `k>=7`.  Write the four non-top plus labels as
`J^epsilon ell`, with low labels `ell=3` for `z` and `ell=1` for the
other three.  A pair supports color two exactly when its two exponents
agree, and color `k-2` exactly when they differ.  If the minus labels
are distinct, each unordered pair supports at most one color, so
`c<=binom(4,2)=6`.

If the minus labels coincide, the two orientations count each active
unordered pair twice.  Let `n_0+n_1=4` be the two exponent counts.
For color two the eligible-pair count is

```text
binom(n_0,2)+binom(n_1,2),
```

and for color `k-2` it is `n_0n_1`.  The complement has the same
simple-current parity for every eligible pair and is invariant only
when the total exponent sum is odd.  In that parity the eligible count
is at most three, again giving `c<=6`.

Finally let `k=6`, so `z=3` is fixed by `J`.  If `t` of the other three
labels are one and the rest five, all eligible pairs among those three
have active complement.  A pair `{3,u}` has active complement in color
two exactly when the other two labels are opposite, and in color four
exactly when they are equal.  For each `t=0,1,2,3`, these contributions
give three active unordered pairs for equal minus labels, hence six
colored edges after doubling the orientation.  For distinct minus
labels there are three colored edges among the cap-two vertices, while
the equal/opposite alternatives at `3` contribute three more.  Thus
again `c<=6`.

Every case contradicts `c=8`.  Hence no `x_i` has cap at least four.
QED.

**Corollary 23A9S2D2 (exact remaining lone-`J` depth columns).**  Under
the hypotheses of Lemma 23A9S2D1, a raw deficit with a minus label of
cap at least four must satisfy

```text
x_i in {1,2,k-2,k-1}                 for every i,
a in {q,k-q},
q,a in {3,4,k-4,k-3}.                              (P23.11z5zy7s11)
```

Thus the only minus depths left by the eight-edge collision column are
four and five.

**Proof.**  Lemma 23A9S2D1 gives the first line.  Part 1 of Lemma
23A9S2D shows that a raw deficit must have `a=q` or `a=Jq`.
Every active pair of labels from `{1,2,J2,J1}` is, after removing its
common simple-current parity, one of

```text
1 star_k 1={0,2},       1 star_k 2={1,3},
2 star_k 2={0,2,4}.
```

Hence any minus label carried by an active edge has cap at most five.
The two minus labels have equal cap when they are equal or
simple-current complements.  Restricting to cap at least four gives
exactly the four displayed labels.  QED.

The finite endpoint columns left by Corollary 23A9S2D2 are already
raw-positive.

**Lemma 23A9S2D3 (lone-`J` collision endpoint closure).**  Retain the
hypotheses of Lemma 23A9S2D1.  Then

```text
T_nt<=N+P_eq.                                      (P23.11z5zy7s12)
```

Thus the two collision columns left open in Lemma 23A9S2D do not require
any additional positive-cut reservoir.

**Proof.**  Lemma 23A9S2D1 gives

```text
x_i in {1,2,k-2,k-1}                  for all four non-`J` plus labels.
```

If both minus labels also have cap at most three, then the cap-three
classification Lemma 23A9U1C applies.  Under the present fusion-depth
hypothesis the two raw-deficit rows of Lemma 23A9U1A are impossible:
one contains the minus label `J`, and the other has both minus labels
`k-1`.  Hence `N+P_eq>=T_nt` in this subcase.

It remains to consider the high-minus columns of Corollary 23A9S2D2.
Write

```text
Jr=k-r.
```

The complete recurrence in these columns gives the following active
composition counts and minimum raw margins.  Here an ``active
composition'' means a weak composition of the four non-`J` plus labels
in `{1,2,J2,J1}` which has at least one active cut and maximal cut rank
at most two.

```text
level range    high-minus columns                 active  min(N+P_eq-T_nt)

k=6            {3,3}                                  9          3

k=7            {3,3},{4,4}                           10         10
               {3,4}                                 12          6

k=8            {3,3},{5,5}                            4         10
               {3,5}                                  5          6
               {4,4}                                  5         14

k>=9           {3,3},{J3,J3}                          4         10
               {3,J3}                                 5          6
               {4,4},{J4,J4}                          2         25
               {4,J4}                                 3         19.       (P23.11z5zy7s13)
```

For `k>=17`, extract the displayed powers of `J`.  Every product needed
for `N`, `P_eq`, and `T_nt` then involves only ordinary labels
`0,1,2,3,4` of total low weight at most sixteen, so the ordinary
Clebsch--Gordan recurrence has no affine-wall term.  This gives the
stable part of `(P23.11z5zy7s13)`.  For `9<=k<=16`, direct use of the
finite rule

```text
N_(a,b)^c=1 iff |a-b|<=c<=min(a+b,2k-a-b)
              and a+b+c is even
```

gives exactly the same grouped rows.  The transition levels `k=6,7,8`
are the first three blocks of `(P23.11z5zy7s13)`.  In every listed
column the minimum raw margin is positive, so the high-minus subcase also
satisfies `(P23.11z5zy7s12)`.  QED.

Away from the first three endpoint columns, the selected active triple
has one additional output-four channel.  This closes the six-edge
one-color residual.

**Lemma 23A9S2E (four-deep profile and one-color normal form).**  Let
`A={r,x,y}` be a non-top active triple in the setting of Lemma
23A9S2.  If

```text
cap_k(x)>=4,                         cap_k(y)>=4,
```

then

```text
(m_0(A),m_2(A),m_4(A))>=(1,2,2).                  (P23.11z5zy7t)
```

Consequently an extended rank-two complementary block gives

```text
N>=2+2*4+2*1=12.                                  (P23.11z5zy7u)
```

Now suppose `k` is absent from `P` and only one colored graph `G_r`
occurs in Lemma 23A9S2C.  If every label incident to an active edge has
cap at least four, then the six-edge extended branch satisfies

```text
T_nt<=12<=N.                                       (P23.11z5zy7v)
```

Apart from the endpoint alternative that some incident label has cap at
most three, every remaining raw deficit in either the weight-one branch
or the all-extended weight-two branch has the following strict graph
normal form:

```text
maximal weight one:       G_r contains K_3 disjoint-union K_2;

maximal weight two,
all cuts extended:        either G_r contains K_3 disjoint-union K_2,
                          or c=7 and
                          G_r=K_2 join independent-set_3.           (P23.11z5zy7w)
```

In the first alternative, write the triangle labels as `x,y,z` and the
remaining active edge as `{u,v}`.  Since all four displayed pairs fuse
to `r`, Lemma 23A9S2C gives an indexed `U_1` supplier as soon as one of

```text
x,y,z in r star_k s.                               (P23.11z5zy7x)
```

Thus absence of this supplier forces all three triangle labels outside
`r star_k s`.  In the exceptional seven-edge graph, write its
three-vertex independent part as `{z_1,z_2,z_3}`.  Its `K_(2,3)`
subgraph and Lemma 23A9S2C similarly give a `U_1` supplier if any
`z_i` lies in `r star_k s`; without one, all three lie outside that
fusion interval.  Hence these two branches are reduced to

```text
an incident label of cap at most three;
an explicit indexed U_1 term;
or one of the two interval-avoidance templates in (P23.11z5zy7w).
                                                               (P23.11z5zy7y)
```

In particular the possible extended `K_(2,3)` at `c=6` is completely
closed away from endpoint cap at most three.

**Proof.**  Put `L=x star_k y`.  It is a contiguous step-two interval,
contains `r`, and has at least four entries.  Formula
`(P23.11z5zy4a)` gives

```text
m_j(A)=|L intersection (r star_k j)|.
```

The output-two intersection contains `r` and at least one adjacent
entry of `L`, so it has size at least two.  We claim that the
output-four intersection contains at least two entries as well.
Otherwise the two step-two intervals `L` and `r star_k 4` meet only at
`r`, so `r` is their pair of opposite endpoints.

If `r` is the lower endpoint of `L` and the upper endpoint of
`r star_k 4`, the latter equality forces `k-r=2`, while the former
forces, after ordering `x<=y`,

```text
y-x=r=k-2.
```

Thus `x<=2`, contrary to `cap_k(x)>=4`.  In the reverse orientation,
`r` is the upper endpoint of `L` and the lower endpoint of
`r star_k 4`.  The latter forces `r=2`; the former says either

```text
x+y=2,                         or 2k-x-y=2,
```

and again one of `x,y` has cap at most three.  This contradiction proves
`(P23.11z5zy7t)`.  The extended complement has

```text
(b_0,b_2,b_4)>=(2,4,1)
```

by Lemma 23A9S2, and dotting the two profiles proves
`(P23.11z5zy7u)`.

In a six-edge extended raw deficit, `(P23.11z5zy7m)` forces every edge
to have weight two.  If its incident labels all have cap at least four,
selecting any edge in `(P23.11z5zy7u)` proves
`(P23.11z5zy7v)`.

It remains to identify the dense graphs.  A
`K_3 disjoint-union K_2` in `G_r` is exactly a bipartition of the
complement graph `H` into independent parts of sizes three and two.
If `G_r` has seven edges, then `H` has three edges.  Unless those edges
form a triangle, `H` is bipartite and its isolated vertices can be
assigned to give parts of sizes three and two.  The sole exception is
therefore

```text
H=K_3 disjoint-union independent-set_2,
```

whose complement is `K_2 join independent-set_3`.  If `G_r` has at
least eight edges, `H` has at most two edges and has the required
bipartition.  After `(P23.11z5zy7v)`, the density floors in Lemma
23A9S2C give `(P23.11z5zy7w)`.

Finally, in a disjoint triangle and edge, the edge `{u,v}` makes
`m(r,u,v)>0`.  Apply the triangle supplier test
`(P23.11z5zy7q1)` at each of `x,y,z`.  In
`K_2 join independent-set_3`, the complete bipartite subgraph
`K_(2,3)` and `(P23.11z5zy7q3)` give the corresponding assertion for
the three-vertex part.  This proves `(P23.11z5zy7x)--(P23.11z5zy7y)`.
QED.

The interval-avoidance templates cannot remain once the complementary
block is three-deep.  The reason is that three entries on each side
already supply the full output-four band needed below.

**Lemma 23A9S2F (three-deep complementary-band closure).**  Let a
selected non-top active cut of maximal complementary rank have

```text
A={r,x,y},                         B={s,u,v,w},
```

and pair the complementary block as two fusion intervals

```text
I=alpha star_k beta,                L=gamma star_k delta
```

with

```text
|I|>=3,               |L|>=3,       d=|I intersection L| in {1,2}.
```

Then its profile satisfies

```text
d=1:       (b_0,b_2,b_4)>=(1,3,6);
d=2:       (b_0,b_2,b_4)>=(2,6,6).                 (P23.11z5zy7z)
```

Since every nonexceptional active triple has profile at least
`(1,2,1)`, orthogonality gives

```text
d=1:                    N>=13;
d=2:                    N>=20.                     (P23.11z5zy7z1)
```

There are also sharp one-step endpoint variants.  Suppose one interval is

```text
I=s star_k ell,             cap_k(s)>=3,            cap_k(ell)=2,
```

the other interval has length at least three, and the invariant
intersection does not contain zero.  Then

```text
d=1:       (b_0,b_2,b_4)>=(1,3,3),                 (P23.11z5zy7z1a0)
d=2:       (b_0,b_2,b_4)>=(2,5,5).                 (P23.11z5zy7z1a)
```

In the rank-two line, if both labels in the selected active pair have
cap at least three, the minimal-profile rigidity
Lemma 23A9S2B2 strengthens its profile in either the output-two or
output-four coordinate, and hence

```text
N>=22.                                             (P23.11z5zy7z1b)
```

Consequently, in the no-`k`, one-color setting the complete non-top
demand is paid whenever one maximal-weight active edge contains every
indexed plus label of cap two.  In either graph template of
`(P23.11z5zy7w)--(P23.11z5zy7y)`, a residual therefore forces the set

```text
L_2={i: cap_k(p_i)=2}
```

to have at least two vertices.  If it has exactly two, every
maximal-weight edge avoids both of them.  In particular the rank-one
chamber has at least three cap-two positions.  Thus the one-color endpoint
is a cap-two weighted-placement problem.  A cap-three inactive minus
label or a cap-three plus label creates no residual by itself.

**Proof.**  Two step-two intervals of length at least three whose
intersection has size at most two meet at opposite ends.  If
`I intersection L={z}`, exchange them so that

```text
z-4,z-2,z in I,                    z,z+2,z+4 in L.
```

The three ordered pairs

```text
(z-2,z),                    (z,z),                 (z,z+2)
```

fuse to output two.  The six ordered pairs

```text
(z-4,z),       (z-2,z),       (z-2,z+2),
(z,z),         (z,z+2),       (z,z+4)
```

fuse to output four.  The displayed interval entries imply
`4<=z<=k-4`, so none of the lower or affine upper triangle inequalities
removes these paths.  This proves the first line of
`(P23.11z5zy7z)`.

If the intersection is `{z,z+2}`, exchange the intervals so that

```text
z-2,z,z+2 in I,                   z,z+2,z+4 in L.
```

The six pairs

```text
(z-2,z),       (z,z),         (z,z+2),
(z+2,z),       (z+2,z+2),     (z+2,z+4)
```

fuse to output two.  The following six pairs fuse to output four:

```text
(z-2,z+2),     (z,z),         (z,z+2),
(z,z+4),       (z+2,z),       (z+2,z+2).
```

Indeed the displayed entries imply `2<=z<=k-4`; the six differences
are at most four, and their sums lie between the output-four walls.
This proves the second line.  Dotting `(P23.11z5zy7z)` with
`(1,2,1)` proves `(P23.11z5zy7z1)`.

There are ten indexed plus pairs.  In a one-color graph, maximal cut
rank one gives total demand at most ten, while maximal cut rank two gives
total demand at most twenty.  Thus `(P23.11z5zy7z1)` pays the complete
one-color demand.

For the endpoint variants, write

```text
I={z,z+2}.
```

The cap assumptions on `s,ell` give `1<=z<=k-3`.  First let the
intersection have rank one.  The other interval meets `I` at one
endpoint and extends away from it by at least two entries.  Up to affine
reflection, it contains

```text
{z-4,z-2,z}.
```

The three pairs

```text
(z,z),                 (z,z-2),                 (z+2,z)
```

fuse to output two, while

```text
(z,z),                 (z,z-2),                 (z,z-4)
```

fuse to output four.  The displayed entries put all sums and
differences inside the finite triangle walls.  This proves
`(P23.11z5zy7z1a0)`.

Now let the intersection have rank two.  The other interval contains
`I` and at least one adjacent entry, hence contains either

```text
{z-2,z,z+2}                 or                 {z,z+2,z+4}.
```

The two cases are exchanged by the affine reflection.  In the second
case the five pairs

```text
(z,z), (z,z+2), (z+2,z), (z+2,z+2), (z+2,z+4)
```

fuse to output two.  Five output-four pairs are

```text
(z,z+2), (z,z+4), (z+2,z), (z+2,z+2), (z+2,z+4).
```

At the sole upper endpoint where the last pair misses output four,
replace it by `(z,z)`; the lower endpoint is already covered.  This
proves `(P23.11z5zy7z1a)`.  Lemma 23A9S2B2 says that the active-triple
profile has `m_2>=3` or `m_4>=2`.  Dotting either alternative with
`(2,5,5)` gives `N>=22`, proving `(P23.11z5zy7z1b)`.

It remains to translate the interval hypothesis into the graph
statement.  Suppose a maximal-weight active edge contains every cap-two
plus position.
Its complementary block contains the other minus label `s` and three
plus labels, all of cap at least three.  Pair `s` with any one of those
labels and pair the other two together.  The exact interval-cardinality
formula

```text
|alpha star_k beta|=min(cap_k(alpha),cap_k(beta))
```

and `cap_k(s)>=3` make both intervals three-deep.  The first part applies.

If `|L_2|=1` and no maximal edge contains its vertex, choose any maximal
edge.  Its active pair has cap at least three, while its complement has
the unique cap-two label and two labels of cap at least three.  Pairing
the other minus label with the cap-two label puts the complement under
`(P23.11z5zy7z1a)--(P23.11z5zy7z1b)`.  Hence this case is also closed.

Finally suppose `|L_2|=2`.  A maximal edge containing both is covered by
the three-deep argument.  A maximal edge containing exactly one has a
nonminimal active triple by Lemma 23A9S2B2, and its complement has exactly
one cap-two label; the endpoint variant again gives `N>=22`.  Therefore
every maximal edge in a residual avoids both cap-two positions.  In the
rank-one chamber all active edges are maximal, while the dense graph has
no isolated vertex, so this is impossible.  The stated placement
conditions follow.  QED.

The weighted cap-two placement residue has an exact unbounded
Presburger classification.  Put

```text
J=k,                 J1=k-1,                 J2=k-2,
J3=k-3,              J5=k-5.
```

**Lemma 23A9S2G (complete no-`J` one-color endpoint).**  Retain the
no-`k`, one-color setting of Lemmas 23A9S2C--23A9S2F, let `r` be the
active color and `s` the inactive minus label, and suppose the density
conditions `(P23.11z5zy7m)` hold.  After the reductions of Lemma
23A9S2F and sorting the five plus labels, the only possible rows are

```text
r    s     plus multiset                  c   h    N   P_eq   T

2    3     {1,1,1,1,1}                  10   0   10    30   10
2    J3    {J1,J1,J1,J1,J1}             10   0   10    30   10

2    5     {1,1,1,3,3}                   9   3   19    16   12
2    J5    {J3,J3,J1,J1,J1}              9   3   19    16   12

J2   3     {1,1,J3,J3,J1}                6   6   21     9   12
J2   J3    {1,3,3,J1,J1}                 6   6   21     9   12.
                                                               (P23.11z5zy7z4)
```

At level seven the third row has `N=18` instead of `19`; rows which
collide with disjoint support or fusion depth at levels six and seven are
simply absent.  Every displayed feasible row satisfies

```text
T<=N+P_eq.                                          (P23.11z5zy7z5)
```

Thus the no-`k`, one-color `d<=2` endpoint is completely closed; it
requires no positive-cut reservoir.

**Proof.**  The classification is an exact symbolic integer calculation,
not a bounded level sweep.  For labels `a,b,t` the verifier uses the
finite fusion predicate

```text
|a-b|<=t<=min(a+b,2k-a-b),             a+b+t even.
                                                               (P23.11z5zy7z6)
```

For a fourfold block `(a,b,c,d)`, put

```text
A_-=|a-b|,       A_+=min(a+b,2k-a-b),
B_-=|c-d|,       B_+=min(c+d,2k-c-d).
```

If `A_-,B_-` have opposite parity its invariant rank is zero; otherwise
it is exactly

```text
max(0, floor((min(A_+,B_+)-max(A_-,B_-))/2)+1).    (P23.11z5zy7z7)
```

The C++ verifier
`character_ring_iter/verify_su2_d12_cap2_z3.cpp` introduces symbolic
integers

```text
k>=6,       2<=r,s<=k-2,       1<=p_1<=...<=p_5<=k-1,
```

imposes disjoint sign support, and defines all twenty oriented cut
booleans from `(P23.11z5zy7z6)--(P23.11z5zy7z7)`.  It requires the
`r`-graph to be nonempty, the `s`-graph to be empty, every active rank
to be at most two, and exactly the necessary density disjunction

```text
h=0 and c>=8,              or              h>0 and c+h>=12.
                                                               (P23.11z5zy7z8)
```

The second branch deliberately includes both the all-extended threshold
twelve and the stronger unextended threshold fourteen, so it does not
discard a possible residual.  Finally it inserts precisely the output of
Lemma 23A9S2F:

```text
|L_2|>=2;
if |L_2|=2, every maximal-weight edge avoids both vertices.
                                                               (P23.11z5zy7z9)
```

All formulas are quantifier-free linear integer arithmetic with parity,
`min`, `max`, and `if-then-else`.  Z3 reports `UNSAT` after adjoining the
negation of the six rows in `(P23.11z5zy7z4)`.  The replay also checks
that the base constraints are satisfiable and that each of the six
symbolic families has a satisfying witness, preventing a vacuous
`UNSAT`.  Hence `(P23.11z5zy7z4)` is exhaustive for every integer
`k>=6`.

Direct substitution in the fusion rule gives the displayed values.  The
two rows in each block are related by applying the simple current to all
five plus labels and to `s`.  The only transition is the value `N=18`
in the third row at `k=7`; from `k=8` onward its low total weight has no
affine truncation.  The three raw margins `N+P_eq-T` are respectively

```text
30,                 22 at k=7 and 23 thereafter,                 18,
```

so every row proves `(P23.11z5zy7z5)`.  QED.

The first three genuine mixed-colour levels are also closed exactly.
This is a finite transition theorem, not the still-needed uniform
mixed-colour argument.

**Lemma 23A9S2H (exact mixed-colour transition levels).**  Retain the
no-`k`, non-top setting of Lemma 23A9S2C, suppose the two minus labels
are distinct and both colours occur, and let the maximal active-cut rank
be at most two.  At levels

```text
k=6,7,8
```

the density alternatives `(P23.11z5zy7m)` imply

```text
T_nt<=N.                                             (P23.11z5zy7z10)
```

More precisely, some active cut `e` with three-leg and four-leg channel
profiles `A_e,B_e` satisfies

```text
sum_(j in {0,2,4}) m_j(A_e)m_j(B_e)>=T_nt.           (P23.11z5zy7z11)
```

**Proof.**  The strict C++ replayer
`character_ring_iter/test_su2_d12_mixed_local_small.cpp` enumerates the
sorted five-label plus multisets with no `k`, the two distinct minus
labels of fusion depth at least three, and all twenty indexed oriented
cuts.  It computes every multiplicity from the exact finite
`SU(2)_k` fusion recurrence, rejects a row if any active rank exceeds
two, requires both colours and precisely the density disjunction

```text
h=0 and c>=8,              or              h>0 and c+h>=12,
```

and checks `(P23.11z5zy7z11)` for all 162 surviving rows.  Across the
selected cut, orthogonality gives

```text
N=sum_(j=0)^k m_j(A_e)m_j(B_e),
```

whose summands are nonnegative; hence `(P23.11z5zy7z11)` implies
`(P23.11z5zy7z10)`.  The replay transcript is
`certificates/su2_d12_mixed_local_small.log`.  QED.

The mixed chamber with no cap-two plus label admits a uniform local
closure.  Its only global input is a sharp thirty-two bound for the
weighted colored graphs.

**Lemma 23A9S2I (uniform mixed three-deep closure).**  Retain the
no-`k`, non-top setting of Lemma 23A9S2C, suppose the two minus labels
are distinct and both colours occur, and let every active rank be at
most two.  If

```text
cap_k(p_i)>=3                 for i=1,...,5,          (P23.11z5zy7z12)
```

then

```text
T_nt<=N.                                             (P23.11z5zy7z13)
```

**Proof.**  First strengthen the active-triple profile.  For an active
cut write

```text
A={r,x,y},                         I=x star_k y.
```

The fusion interval `I` has at least three entries and contains `r`.
Also `cap_k(r)>=3`.  Intersecting `I` with `r star_k 2` and
`r star_k 4` gives

```text
m_0(A)=1,             m_2(A)>=2,             m_4(A)>=2,
m_2(A)>=3             or                      m_4(A)>=3.
                                                        (P23.11z5zy7z14)
```

Indeed, away from the two depth-three walls, `r star_k 4` contains the
two step-two neighbours of `r` in either direction, so any three-entry
subinterval of `I` through `r` contributes three output-four paths.  At
`r=2` or `r=k-2`, the sole way to lose the second neighbour in the
output-four interval makes `I` contain all three entries of
`r star_k 2`.  This proves both the lower bounds and the final
alternative in `(P23.11z5zy7z14)`.

For the complementary block pair the other minus label with any one of
its three plus labels and pair the remaining two plus labels together.
All four labels have cap at least three.  Lemma 23A9S2F therefore gives

```text
d=1:       (b_0,b_2,b_4)>=(1,3,6),
d=2:       (b_0,b_2,b_4)>=(2,6,6).                  (P23.11z5zy7z15)
```

Dotting `(P23.11z5zy7z14)` with `(P23.11z5zy7z15)` yields

```text
d=2:                         N>=32.                 (P23.11z5zy7z16)
```

If every active cut has rank one, there are only twenty indexed

**Lemma 23A9S2J (uniform mixed one-cap closure).**  Retain the genuine

Now suppose a rank-two cut occurs and select one.  Corollary

If its pair avoids the cap-two label, use the active alternative

**Lemma 23A9S2K (complete mixed three-cap closure).**  Retain the

```text
2       3       {1,1,1,4,4}                     22          13
```

**Proof.**  Exhaustiveness and the `T_nt` column are further exact

Their output-one and output-three counts are `2m` and `4m-3`, so again

The three plus positions of cap at least three support only

```text
m_2(A)>=3                 or                 m_4(A)>=2,
```

and in either case `N>=13`.  If the active pair contains both cap-two

Now suppose a rank-two cut occurs.  The 256-parity cap-placement
verifier of Lemma 23A9S2I proves one further exact implication:

```text
n_2=2, h>0, density
   implies a rank-two active edge containing exactly one
           cap-two plus position.                  (P23.11z5zy7z23)
```

Indeed
`character_ring_iter/verify_su2_d12_mixed_caps_z3.cpp` adjoins the
negation of `(P23.11z5zy7z23)` to the same exact activity and
rank-at-most-two formulas used in `(P23.11z5zy7z17)`; the result is

```text
k=9,          (q,a)=(3,5),          P={1,1,4,4,4}
```

has colour counts `(6,6)`, demand `24`, and such an edge, so this added
branch is nonvacuous.

Order the two minus labels as `q<a`.  Among the edges supplied by
`(P23.11z5zy7z23)`, select a `q`-coloured edge if one exists; otherwise
select an `a`-coloured edge.  Relabel its cap endpoint as `p_0`, its
three-deep endpoint as `p_1`, the other cap endpoint as `p_4`, and sort
the remaining two three-deep positions `p_2<=p_3`.  There are exactly
four endpoint schemas:

```text
(p_0,p_4)=(1,1), (k-1,k-1), (1,k-1), (k-1,1).       (P23.11z5zy7z24)
```

The strict C++ verifier
`character_ring_iter/verify_su2_d12_mixed_n2_z3.cpp` checks the local
inequality for this selected edge.  For clarity, its exact formula is
recorded here.  If

```text
I=a star_k b=[A_-,A_+]_2,       L=c star_k d=[B_-,B_+]_2,
```

then for `t in {0,2,4}` the coefficient of `V_t` in
`V_a V_b V_c V_d` is the sum, over
`delta=-t,-t+2,...,t`, of the step-two integers `x` satisfying

```text
A_-<=x<=A_+,               B_- - delta<=x<=B_+ - delta,
(t-delta)/2<=x<=k-(t+delta)/2,
x=A_- (mod 2),             x+delta=B_- (mod 2).     (P23.11z5zy7z25)
```

This is exact: put `y=x+delta`; the displayed bounds are precisely
`x in I`, `y in L`, and the lower and affine upper triangle
inequalities for `N_(x,y)^t=1`.  The active three-leg coefficient is
the corresponding intersection of two binary fusion intervals.
Consequently the verifier computes exactly

```text
L_e=sum_(t in {0,2,4}) m_t(A_e)m_t(B_e).             (P23.11z5zy7z26)
```

It writes all eight labels as `2z+epsilon`, checks all 256 parity

priority rule.  The simultaneous counterexample condition

is `UNSAT` in all `4*2*256=2048` queries.  The row

```text
k=13,          (q,a)=(4,6),          P={8,8,8,12,12}
```

has `T_nt=27`; its indicated `q`- and `a`-coloured local bounds are
respectively `32` and `26`.  The verifier checks these values directly,
so the colour priority is both necessary for this local rule and
nonvacuous.  Finally orthogonality across the selected cut gives

```text
N=sum_(t=0)^k m_t(A_e)m_t(B_e)>=L_e>=T_nt,
```

which proves `(P23.11z5zy7z22)`.  The replay transcript is
`certificates/su2_d12_mixed_n2_z3.log`.  QED.

**Corollary 23A9S2M (complete uniform mixed no-`k` closure).**  Retain

The preceding endpoint analysis has a shorter direct consolidation.  It
is useful independently of the endpoint packets because it keeps the
global invariant, the equal-pair terms, and the positive cuts in three
disjoint summands.

**Lemma 23A9S2N (canonical direct-payment reduction at rank at most
two).**  Retain the disjoint-support hypotheses of Proposition 23A9S and
suppose every indexed negative cut has rank at most two.  If `T>0`,
choose a maximal indexed cut and write its two factorization blocks as
`A|B`, with three and four tensor factors respectively.  Put

```text
L_4(A|B)=sum_(t in {0,2,4})       m_t(A)m_t(B),
L_8(A|B)=sum_(t in {0,2,4,6,8})   m_t(A)m_t(B).       (P23.11z5zy7z28)
```

For each indexed equal pair `E` among the five plus positions, put
`ell=|q-a|` and retain only the first two binary channels in its
`P_eq` contribution:

```text
P_2=sum_(E equal)
       {m_ell(P minus E)
        +indicator_(ell+2 in q star_k a)m_(ell+2)(P minus E)}.
                                                               (P23.11z5zy7z29)
```

Then

```text
L_4<=L_8<=N,             P_2<=P_eq-indicator_(q=a)m(P),          (P23.11z5zy7z30)
```

and an active cut with `q=a` has `m(P)>=1`.  Consequently either one
of the following local inequalities proves the complete signed
contraction:

```text
L_4+P_2+U+indicator_(q=a) >= T,     if a minus label has cap <=2,
L_8+P_2+U+indicator_(q=a) >= T,     if both minus caps are at least 3.
                                                               (P23.11z5zy7z31)
```

Moreover, the negations of `(P23.11z5zy7z31)` have the following finite,
cutoff-free QF-LIA covers.

```text
shallow: 7 minus types * 2 level parities * 32 plus parity masks
         * 2 selected orientations = 896 cells;

deep:    (2 distinct selected orientations + 1 equal orientation)
         * 2 level parities * 2 q parities * 32 plus parity masks
         * 2 selected ranks = 768 cells.             (P23.11z5zy7z32)
```

Here the seven shallow types are the four sorted distinct possibilities

```text
(1,a),       (q,k-1),       (q,k),       (k-1,k),
```

with the overlaps removed in that order, and the three equal
possibilities

```text
(1,1),       (k-1,k-1),       (k,k).
```

In the deep cover `2<=q<=a<=k-2`; the two kinds are `q<a` and `q=a`.
Thus UNSAT in every cell of the two covers implies `(P23.11z5zy)` for
every seven-factor two-minus word whose maximal negative-cut rank is at
most two.

**Proof.**  Orthogonality across the selected cut gives

```text
N=sum_(t=0)^k m_t(A)m_t(B),
```

with nonnegative integer summands, proving the first half of
`(P23.11z5zy7z30)`.  Deleting an indexed equal plus pair leaves the
fivefold invariant

```text
m(q,a,P minus E)
  =sum_(t in q star_k a)m_t(P minus E).
```

The first two terms are exactly `(P23.11z5zy7z29)`, proving its stated
lower bound.  If `q=a` and the selected cut is active, its selected plus
pair and complementary plus triple both have a channel to `q`.  Fusing
those two channels through `V_q tensor V_q -> V_0` gives `m(P)>=1`.
The three retained reservoirs belong respectively to `N`, the indexed
equal-plus part of `P_eq`, and `U`; the last unit belongs to the
equal-minus part of `P_eq`.  Hence no summand is reused, and either
inequality in `(P23.11z5zy7z31)` implies Proposition 23A9S.

It remains only to justify the finite covers.  A positive label has cap
at most two exactly when it is `1,k-1`, or `k`; sorting the two minus
labels gives the seven displayed shallow types.  Otherwise both lie in
`[2,k-2]`, giving the two deep kinds.  Total fusion parity determines
the omitted minus-label parity from the five plus parities.  The
stabilizer of a selected plus pair sorts that pair and its complementary
triple.  For distinct minus labels it leaves two orientations, according
to which minus label lies in the selected triple; for equal labels the
orientations coincide.  Finally a positive maximal rank is one or two.
These observations give `(P23.11z5zy7z32)` and lose no integer chamber.

The verifier formulas are exact QF-LIA.  Binary fusion is the pair of
triangle walls with its parity congruence; fourfold multiplicity is the
intersection count of two step-two fusion intervals.  For fixed
`t<=8`, a threefold coefficient is at most `t+1`, so its product with
the complementary coefficient is represented without nonlinear
arithmetic by the bounded repeated-sum formula.  Thus each solver cell
is precisely the negation asserted above.  QED.

**Corollary 23A9S2N1 (complete uniform shallow-minus rank-two
closure).**  Under the hypotheses of Proposition 23A9S, suppose every
negative-cut rank is at most two and at least one of the two minus
labels has cap at most two.  Then

```text
T<=N+P_eq+U.                                         (P23.11z5zy7z33)
```

Hence every such seven-factor contraction is nonnegative in every
`SU(2)_k`.

**Proof.**  If `T=0` the assertion is immediate.  Otherwise choose a
maximal active indexed cut and apply the shallow alternative of Lemma
23A9S2N.  The strict C++ verifier

```text
character_ring_iter/verify_su2_d12_shallow_minus_z3.cpp
```

checks the 896 exhaustive cells in `(P23.11z5zy7z32)`.  Every negated
local inequality is `UNSAT`, so `(P23.11z5zy7z31)` holds and

```text
certificates/su2_d12_shallow_minus_z3.log.
```

Its source SHA-256 is
`5f0c32515244ab1ed3360f7119efdf3a2d0cbee83fabbaea535b2cabdcab9e9d`.

The ordinary straightening target `kappa<=P_eq` does not pass unchanged
through the affine wall.  The obstruction is an unbounded simple-current
family, not a low-level accident.

**Lemma 23A9T (simple-current kernel and positive-cut payment).**  For every
`k>=7`, take the two minus labels and five plus labels

```text
(q,a)=(k,3),
P=[1,2,k-3,k-2,k-1].                                (P23.11z5zz1)
```

All seven labels are distinct, so `P_eq=0` in Proposition 23A9S.  Let
`O_-` be the direct sum of the negative `3|4` factorization spaces counted
by `T`, and let

```text
mu_-:O_- -> Inv(V_q tensor V_a tensor product_(p in P)V_p)
```

be tensor multiplication.  Then

```text
dim ker(mu_-)>=1>P_eq.                               (P23.11z5zz2)
```

The same relation has a unit of positive-cut supply:

```text
U>=m(k,3,k-3)m(1,k-1,2,k-2)>=1.                     (P23.11z5zz3)
```

Consequently a wall-uniform kernel proof of `(P23.11z5zy)` must retain
`U`; the stronger target `dim ker(mu_-)<=P_eq` is false even with pairwise
distinct labels.  Indeed, writing `kappa_k=dim ker(mu_-)`, rank-nullity
gives

```text
T=rank(mu_-)+kappa_k<=N+kappa_k.
```

Thus

```text
kappa_k<=P_eq+U                                      (P23.11z5zz6)
```

is the corrected finite sufficient kernel target.  The ordinary
straightening target `kappa_infinity<=P_eq` remains viable; Lemma 23A9T
shows precisely why its finite analogue needs the additional positive-cut
term.

**Proof.**  Put `J=V_k`.  It is the order-two simple current, and

```text
N_(r,k-r)^k=1,             J star_k J=V_0.           (P23.11z5zz4)
```

Thus every complementary pair has a unique channel to `J`.  Consider the
two distinct negative cuts

```text
A_1={k,1,k-1},             A_2={k,2,k-2}.            (P23.11z5zz5)
```

Each triple is invariant: fuse its complementary pair to `J` and then use
`J star_k J=V_0`.  Each four-element complement is invariant as well.  For
`A_1`, fuse `(2,k-2)` and `(3,k-3)` separately to `J`, then fuse the two
copies of `J` to the unit; the argument for `A_2` is identical.

More precisely, fuse each of the three pairs

```text
(1,k-1),             (2,k-2),             (3,k-3)
```

to `J`, retain the external `J=V_k`, and fuse the resulting four simple
currents to the unit.  This gives a nonzero global invariant `w`.  Grouping
the same fusion tree first across `A_1|A_1^c` shows that `w` lies in the
image of the `A_1` source block; grouping it across `A_2|A_2^c` shows that
it lies in the other image.  All relevant simple-current morphism spaces
are one-dimensional and their associators are invertible, so the two
source vectors have proportional nonzero images.  Their appropriate
difference is a nonzero element of `ker(mu_-)`, proving
`(P23.11z5zz2)`.

Finally `(k,3,k-3)` is an invariant triple, while
`(1,k-1,2,k-2)` is invariant by the same two-pair construction.  This is
the displayed summand of the first sum defining `U`, and proves
`(P23.11z5zz3)`.  QED.

The positive summand in Lemma 23A9T does not merely have sufficient
dimension: it supplies the literal Temperley--Lieb boundary of the
displayed wall relation.

**Corollary 23A9U (simple-current three-term subcomplex).**  In the family
`(P23.11z5zz1)`, choose the one-dimensional fusion paths

```text
x_1 in Inv(k,1,k-1) tensor Inv(3,2,k-3,k-2),
x_2 in Inv(k,2,k-2) tensor Inv(3,1,k-3,k-1),

u in Inv(k,3,k-3) tensor Inv(1,k-1,2,k-2)            (P23.11z5zz7)
```

which fuse each complementary pair `(r,k-r)` through the simple current
`J=V_k`.  After nonzero scalar normalization, multiplication gives the
same global invariant `w` on all three paths.  The recoupling maps therefore
form an exact complex

```text
0 -> span{u} --d_2--> span{x_1,x_2} --d_1--> span{w} -> 0,

d_2(u)=x_1-x_2,               d_1(x_1)=d_1(x_2)=w.   (P23.11z5zz8)
```

Thus this unbounded affine kernel line is paid by the specific unit of
positive-cut supply in `(P23.11z5zz3)`.

**Proof.**  Every indicated morphism space used to build the three vectors
is one-dimensional.  In each case, forgetting the first cut and
associating the four copies of `J` gives the same nonzero morphism

```text
J star_k J star_k J star_k J -> 1.
```

All `F`-moves are invertible, so each multiplication image is a nonzero
scalar multiple of this morphism.  Rescale `x_1,x_2,u` to make the three
images equal to `w`.  The displayed formulas then give
`d_1d_2=0`; `d_2` is injective, `d_1` is surjective, and
`ker(d_1)=span{x_1-x_2}=image(d_2)`.  QED.

The positive-cut term is also indispensable for the numerical inequality,
not only for the kernel estimate.  The obstruction already has maximal
negative-cut rank two.

**Lemma 23A9U1 (unbounded rank-two positive-cut payment).**  For every
`k>=5`, take

```text
q=a=1,
P=[2,k-2,k-1,k-1,k].                              (P23.11z5zz8a)
```

In the notation of Proposition 23A9S, split `U=U_1+U_2` according to its
one-plus and two-plus sums.  Then

```text
N=6,        P_eq=4,        U_1=1,        U_2=3,
T=12.                                                    (P23.11z5zz8b)
```

There are eight active indexed oriented negative cuts and their maximal
contribution is `d=2`.  Consequently

```text
N+P_eq-T=-2,             N+P_eq+U-T=2.              (P23.11z5zz8c)
```

Thus even the actual finite seven-factor inequality in the small-cut
chamber cannot in general be proved after discarding `U`.

**Proof.**  Put `J=V_k`, `e=k-1=J star_k 1`, and
`h=k-2=J star_k 2`.  Since `J star_k J=V_0`, an even number of
simultaneous `J` twists can be removed from an invariant multiplicity.
The only low products needed below are

```text
1 star_k 1=0+2,             2 star_k 2=0+2+4.       (P23.11z5zz8d)
```

They are unchanged for `k>=5`.  Removing the four `J` twists in the
plus list gives

```text
N=m(1,1,1,1,2,2)=6.
```

The equal-minus term of `P_eq` is `m(P)=m(1,1,2,2)=2`.  The only equal
plus pair is the indexed pair `{e,e}`; deleting it gives another
`m(1,1,2,2)=2`.  Hence `P_eq=4`.

In the one-plus part of `U`, the triple `m(1,1,p_i)` is nonzero only at
the label `p_i=2`.  Its complementary block is `{h,e,e,J}` and has
multiplicity one, so `U_1=1`.  In the two-plus part, the only nonzero
products are

```text
E={h,J}:       m(1,1,h,J)m(2,e,e)=1,
E={e,e}:       m(1,1,e,e)m(2,h,J)=2.                (P23.11z5zz8e)
```

Thus `U_2=3`.

It remains to count `T`.  In either of its identical minus
orientations, the two indexed pairs `{h,e}` have complementary
multiplicity

```text
m(1,2,e,J)=1,
```

while the two indexed pairs `{e,J}` have complementary multiplicity

```text
m(1,2,h,e)=m(1,1,2,2)=2.
```

Their triple factors are all one.  Every other indexed pair has zero
triple factor or zero complementary factor; this follows directly from
the two finite Clebsch--Gordan intervals, including the endpoint `k=5`.
Each orientation therefore contributes `2*1+2*2=6`.  Hence `T=12`,
there are eight active oriented cuts, and their largest contribution is
two.  This proves all assertions.  QED.

There are two further unbounded rank-two packets once the minus labels are
allowed to leave the fundamental column.  One is the numerical Q3 profile
behind the one-import obstruction of Lemma 23A9G.

**Lemma 23A9U1A (nonfundamental simple-current rank-two packets).**  For
`k>=5`, put

```text
J=k,                 e=k-1,                 h=k-2.
```

The following two signed lists have the exact profiles shown:

```text
minus       plus                 N   P_eq   U_1   U_2   T   c   d
{h,J}       {1,1,2,e,e}          6     4     2     2   12   8   2
{e,e}       {1,1,2,h,J}          6     4     1     3   12   8   2.  (P23.11z5zz8n)
```

Thus both families satisfy

```text
N+P_eq-T=-2,                 N+P_eq+U-T=2.           (P23.11z5zz8o)
```

In particular, the positive-cut reservoir pays both nonfundamental
simple-current families uniformly in the level.

**Proof.**  Write `J=V_k`, `e=J star_k 1`, and `h=J star_k 2`.
Removing the four simultaneous `J` twists in either sevenfold invariant
gives

```text
N=m(1,1,1,1,2,2)=6.                                (P23.11z5zz8p)
```

For the first row of `(P23.11z5zz8n)`, the two indexed equal-plus pairs
`{1,1}` and `{e,e}` each contribute
`m(1,1,2,2)=2` to `P_eq`.  The sole nonzero one-plus term is

```text
p_i=2:             m(h,J,2)m(1,1,e,e)=1*2.
```

The only nonzero two-plus terms are

```text
E={1,1}:           m(h,J,1,1)m(2,e,e)=1*1,
E={e,e}:           m(h,J,e,e)m(1,1,2)=1*1.          (P23.11z5zz8q)
```

This gives `(P_eq,U_1,U_2)=(4,2,2)`.  The only active negative
pairs are the four indexed choices `{1,e}`.  With minus orientation `h`
their triple and complementary ranks are `(1,1)`; with orientation `J`
they are `(1,2)`.  Hence

```text
T=4*(1+2)=12,
```

with four rank-one and four rank-two oriented cuts.

For the second row, the equal-minus term and the indexed equal-plus pair
`{1,1}` each contribute `m(1,1,2,2)=2` to `P_eq`.  Its nonzero positive
terms are

```text
U_1:  p_i=2,        1*1,
U_2:  E={1,1},      2*1,
      E={h,J},      1*1.                            (P23.11z5zz8r)
```

Thus `(P_eq,U_1,U_2)=(4,1,3)`.  For each of the two identical minus
orientations, the two indexed pairs `{1,h}` have ranks `(1,1)` and the
two indexed pairs `{1,J}` have ranks `(1,2)`.  Therefore

```text
T=2*2*1+2*2*2=12,
```

again with four cuts of each rank.

All unlisted factors vanish by the finite Clebsch--Gordan intervals.  In
the first row the only extra endpoint possibility is `{1,2}` at `k=5`;
its complement is `m(J,1,e,e)=0`, since this is the multiplicity of `J`
in `1 star_k 1 star_k 1` and `k=5>3`.  Thus the tables hold already at
the stated endpoint `k=5`.  Equations `(P23.11z5zz8p)`--`(P23.11z5zz8r)`
now prove every entry of `(P23.11z5zz8n)` and hence
`(P23.11z5zz8o)`.  QED.

The low levels contain a few further isolated raw deficits.  Their payment
can be recorded without treating a bounded enumeration as a chamber
classification.

**Proof.**  At a fixed level the binary rule is

```text
N_(a,b)^c=1 iff
 |a-b|<=c<=min(a+b,2k-a-b) and a+b+c is even.        (P23.11z5zz8t)
```

Multiply the seven labels along any fixed bracketing for `N`; delete the

`U_1,U_2,T`.  Rule `(P23.11z5zz8t)` gives respectively the seven rows

```text
(N,P_eq,U_1,U_2; rank-one cuts,rank-two cuts)
 =(6,5,2,4;8,4), (6,5,2,8;12,0),

  (9,4,3,4;6,4), (7,3,2,2;7,2).
```

Summing the cut ranks gives the displayed `T`, and direct subtraction

The stable cap-three endpoint sector has an exact finite classification.
